https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Transformation opens doors for local businesses
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Local firms have been given the chance to put themselves at the front of the queue for future work linked to London Stansted's major transformation programme after taking part in the airport's annual Meet the Buyers event.
More than 140 businesses met face-to-face with 30 buyers and procurement specialists at the event, which connects companies with organisations looking for new suppliers and partners.
A total of 700 one-to-one meetings took place during the event, with businesses from sectors including construction, engineering, facilities management, logistics and professional services taking part.
Held at the Radisson Blu Hotel, this year's event marked the 25th anniversary of Meet the Buyers, which was launched by London Stansted and has helped generate more than £37 million of business opportunities for companies across the East of England over the past 15 years alone.
The event comes as London Stansted progresses its five-year transformation programme, a major investment project that includes extending the existing terminal and creating a bright, spacious environment with new shops, bars and restaurants.
The programme will support the airport's long-term growth plans, enabling London Stansted to serve up to 51 million passengers a year without the need for a new runway. It will also create opportunities for businesses across the airport's supply chain.
Marcella M'Rabety, Head of Social Sustainability at London Stansted, said:
"London Stansted is investing in its future and we want local businesses to be part of that journey. Our transformation programme will create opportunities across a wide range of sectors, and Meet the Buyers helps ensure local companies are well placed to benefit from that investment."By bringing businesses together with buyers and decision-makers, we're helping more of the economic value generated by the airport to be shared across our local communities and the wider region."
A mong those attending was Gary Blair, Head of Supply Chain at Farrans Ltd, who said:
"Meet the Buyers was a valuable opportunity to connect with suppliers, subcontractors and industry partners from across the region. We made a number of positive connections and look forward to building on those relationships in the future."
Local firms also used the event to explore potential opportunities linked to the airport's future growth plans.
Vaida Markeviciene, of Bishop's Stortford-based AVM Workwear & Embroidery, said:
"It was a busy day with lots of opportunities to make new contacts and discuss potential contracts. Events like this give smaller businesses the chance to get in front of organisations and buyers they might not otherwise meet."
Since launching in 2001, Meet the Buyers has become one of the region's longest-running business networking events. The initiative has since been adopted by Manchester and East Midlands airports and has generated more than £78 million of opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses across the UK.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: London Stansted to conduct major emergency training exercise
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
An emergency training exercise designed to test London Stansted’s response to a major aircraft accident will take place next week as part of the airport's regular preparedness programme.
The exercise will be held on Tuesday 24 November and forms part of the airport's four-year regulatory testing programme. The exercise is required under Civil Aviation Authority regulations, which require UK certificated aerodromes to undertake a full-scale aircraft accident exercise at least once every four years.
Local residents and passengers are being advised in advance of the exercise, so they are not alarmed on the day by the high number of emergency service vehicles in the area.
The scenario will simulate an aircraft accident requiring a complex, prolonged, multi-agency response and is designed to test life-saving procedures, command and control arrangements, communications, and support processes for passengers, families and stakeholders.
The exercise will take place at the airport's Compass Base facility, a remote aircraft parking stand, using a decommissioned aircraft and has been carefully planned to ensure there is no impact on flight operations or passengers using the airport. A number of emergency service vehicles and personnel will be visible in the area during the exercise.
Around 400 participants will take part, including teams from across London Stansted, alongside colleagues from Essex Police, Essex County Fire & Rescue Service, East of England Ambulance Service and Essex & Herts Air Ambulance.
Also supporting the exercise will be the British Red Cross, Uttlesford District Council, Essex County Council, the Rapid Relief Team, the Air Accident Investigation Branch, the Ministry of Housing, Communities & Local Government, Ryanair, Border Force and National Express.
Nick Millar, Operations Director at London Stansted Airport, said:
"The safety and security of our passengers, colleagues and airport community is always our highest priority.
"Although an aircraft accident is an extremely unlikely event, it remains the most significant emergency scenario we could face, which is why it is vital that we regularly test our plans, procedures and response capabilities.
"The exercise will bring together airport teams, emergency services and partner organisations from across the region, giving us the opportunity to rehearse how we would work together in a highly challenging situation and identify any opportunities to strengthen our response arrangements.
"We want to reassure passengers, local residents and businesses that this is only a training exercise and there will be no impact on the airport's day-to-day operations. However, people in the area may notice increased activity from emergency service vehicles and personnel on the day."
Essex Police Chief Inspector Julia Finch, Stansted Airport Commander , said:
"We regularly test our plans and capabilities, and this is no exception.
"Taking part in these exercises are really important to ensure we are ready for any eventuality, no matter how unlikely the scenario.
"We have a really positive working relationship with Stansted Airport and we’re grateful for this opportunity."
The exercise is designed to provide assurance that emergency plans, facilities, people and partner organisations can work effectively together under realistic conditions and operational pressures, in addition to fulfilling the airport's regulatory requirements.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: East of England tops regional export growth rankings
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
·       Six in ten exporters increased overseas sales in Q3 — the highest proportion among the four regions covered
·       42% entered a new overseas market, joint highest alongside London
·       US leads the region’s overseas growth markets, followed by France and Australia
The East of England recorded the highest proportion of firms growing overseas sales in the last quarter, according to the latest UK Trade Barometer.
Six in 10 exporters (60%) said they increased sales to existing overseas markets in Q3, ahead of London (59%), the Midlands (55%) and the North (53%), and above the UK-wide figure of 53%.
The region also shared the top spot for breaking into new markets - 42% of East of England exporters started trading in a new overseas territory, level with London and six percentage points above the national figure of 36%.
The Barometer — from the UK’s largest airports group and London Stansted owner, MAG, and the Growing Together Alliance of business groups — surveys more than 2,000 businesses through YouGov every quarter about their export performance over the past three months and their expectations for the quarter ahead.
The US was the leading market for the East of England on both measures. Almost one in five exporters (19%) reported growing sales to America, with the same proportion entering the US market for the first time.
France was the next most frequently cited market for increased sales, at 10%, followed by Australia (7%) and Spain (6%). Belgium, Canada, Germany, Poland, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates were each identified by 4% of the region’s exporters.
For new-market entry, France again ranked second, with 9% of exporters starting to trade there, followed by Australia at 4%.
Looking ahead, one in five businesses across the East of England (20%) expect to increase sales to an existing overseas market by the end of December 2026, while 11% expect to start trading in a new market.
Those figures are below the UK-wide averages of 24% and 16% respectively, showing that the region’s strong recent export performance is not yet matched by above-average expectations for the quarter ahead.
It comes after separate data produced for London Stansted by WPI Economics, revealed the East of England continues to go from strength to strength with international services trade in the region growing by 96% between 2016 and 2023. Growth was particularly strong beyond the EU, where services trade increased by 112%.
London Stansted’s Managing Director, Gareth Powell , said:
“Businesses succeed when they can connect easily with customers, suppliers and markets around the world. The latest MAG Trade Barometer highlights the strength of the East of England's international trading community, with 60% of exporters increasing sales in existing overseas markets during Q3 and 42% successfully entering new markets, making the region one of the UK's strongest performers.
"From established markets such as the US and France to emerging opportunities around the world, businesses depend on strong international connections to grow and compete. London Stansted's extensive route network and significant cargo operation help provide those vital links, supporting trade, investment and economic growth across the East of England."
Dan Thorp, Chief Executive at Cambridge Ahead, said:
“The latest figures highlight the strength of the East of England's business base, and the leading role it plays for the UK economy on the global stage.
“With the East of England reporting the highest increase in overseas sales alongside the top spot for breaking into new markets, it is clear that our region stands out for being internationally connected and active.
“International connectivity is a vital component of the Cambridge economy, which operates at the forefront of highly international and competitive innovation sectors, and these results show why investment into the Cambridge and East of England economy are so important for the UK in a global context"

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Business event marks 25 years of helping local firms win contracts
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
A business networking event set up by London Stansted to help local companies win new work is celebrating its 25th anniversary.
Meet the Buyers, which takes place this week (19 Nov) at the Radisson Blu Hotel, has spent 25 years connecting small businesses with major employers, contractors and procurement teams looking for new suppliers.
Since launching in 2001, the event has helped hundreds of firms from across Essex and the East of England showcase their products and services and compete for new contracts.
Over the past 15 years alone, the event has helped businesses across London and the East of England secure more than £37 million worth of new business opportunities.
The success of the scheme has also led to it being rolled out at Manchester and East Midlands airports, with the programme generating more than £78 million in opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses nationwide.
The event works a bit like business speed dating, giving firms a chance to meet buyers from large organisations in a series of short face-to-face meetings that can lead to contracts, partnerships and long-term commercial relationships.
This year's event will bring together businesses and buyers from sectors including construction, engineering, facilities management, logistics and professional services.
Marcella M'Rabety, Head of Social Sustainability, said:
"We're incredibly proud to be celebrating 25 years of Meet the Buyers and the impact the event has had on businesses across our region. For a quarter of a century it has helped bring local companies together with major organisations, creating valuable connections and opening doors to new opportunities.
"Over the past 15 years alone, those opportunities have translated into more than £37 million of business for companies across London and the East of England. As the airport continues to grow and invest, we want local businesses to be part of that journey and benefit from the opportunities it creates."
The event forms part of London Stansted's wider efforts to support economic growth in the region by helping local businesses find new customers, expand and create jobs.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: New Bond, new adventures: Step into the world of 007
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
The world’s most famous secret agent has a new face, with British actor Robert Pattinson confirmed as the next James Bond, taking over the role from Daniel Craig.
And while film fans wait to see what adventures await the new 007, there are plenty of opportunities to follow in the footsteps of his predecessors, with many of the locations made famous by the franchise just a short flight from London Stansted.
From the sun-soaked streets of Italy to the spectacular mountain scenery of Switzerland, the Bond films have showcased some of Europe’s most memorable destinations over more than six decades.
Several are easily accessible from Stansted, offering inspiration for a different kind of city break or European getaway.
The airport even has its own place in Bond history.
In Tomorrow Never Dies, Stansted doubled as Hamburg Airport, where Q introduces Bond to his gadget packed BMW, famously equipped with remote-control technology.
The scenes featuring Pierce Brosnan and Desmond Llewelyn were shot inside one of Stansted's hangars in 1997.
Among the destinations where travellers can retrace 007’s footsteps are:
Italy - From Matera’s ancient streets to Venice’s canals
Italy has provided the backdrop for some of Bond’s most memorable adventures.
The ancient city of Matera featured prominently in No Time to Die, with its spectacular Sassi cave dwellings providing the setting for the film’s opening Aston Martin DB5 chase.
Venice’s romantic waterways featured in both Casino Royale and Moonraker, while Rome’s historic streets provided the setting for the spectacular car chase in Spectre. Lake Como also featured in Casino Royale, with its elegant lakeside villas.
France - Paris and beyond
Paris featured in A View to a Kill, with its famous landmarks providing the setting for one of the franchise’s most memorable action sequences.
Nearby Château de Chantilly also doubled as the estate of villain Max Zorin.
easyJet launched its direct London Stansted to Paris service in March 2026, making the French capital another option for Bond inspired travellers.
Austria - A spectacular Alpine backdrop
Vienna played host to memorable scenes in The Living Daylights, including Bond’s encounter with Kara at the city’s famous Wiener Riesenrad, the giant Ferris wheel at Prater amusement park.
Further west, the picturesque Alpine village of Obertilliach featured in Spectre, providing the dramatic setting for Bond’s plane crash landing during a high-speed mountain pursuit.
Turkey - Istanbul’s big-screen history
Istanbul has featured in several Bond adventures, most notably From Russia With Love, which showcased the city’s historic mosques, bustling markets and waterways.
Maiden’s Tower, standing on a small island in the Bosphorus, also featured in The World Is Not Enough, serving as the hideaway of Elektra King.
Turkish Airlines launched its London Stansted to Istanbul service in March 2026, offering up to 15 flights a week.
Switzerland - Where Bond takes on the mountains
Few countries have provided a more dramatic setting for 007 than Switzerland.
The spectacular Furka Pass featured in Goldfinger, providing the backdrop for the legendary Aston Martin DB5 chase, while the Swiss Alps have featured in several other films, including On Her Majesty’s Secret Service.
Switzerland also provided the setting for one of Bond’s most spectacular stunts in GoldenEye, when Pierce Brosnan’s 007 made his debut with a 220-metre bungee jump from the Verzasca Dam.
Germany - Bond’s connection to Hamburg
Hamburg featured in Tomorrow Never Dies, with the city’s streets providing the backdrop for Bond’s mission against media tycoon Elliot Carver.
The film also has a special connection to London Stansted, where one of the airport’s hangars doubled as Hamburg Airport in the scenes where Q introduces Bond to his remote controlled BMW.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Transport forum marks milestone as public transport use hits 14 million
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
More passengers than ever are choosing public transport to travel to and from London Stansted, with more than 13.5 million travelling by rail, bus and coach over the past 12 months.
Almost half of all passengers now travel to and from the airport by public transport, giving Stansted the highest public transport mode share of any major UK airport.
The figures were revealed as the Stansted Airport Transport Forum celebrated its 25th anniversary, marking a quarter of a century of bringing together transport operators, local authorities, businesses and community organisations to improve connections to the airport.
When the forum was established, Stansted handled around nine million passengers a year and around a third travelled by public transport.
Rail continues to play a growing role in connecting passengers with the airport, with its mode share now exceeding 35%.
Recent developments include a successful trial of 24-hour Stansted Express services, the opening of Cambridge South station and the introduction of contactless ticketing.
The airport's coach and bus network has also expanded over the past year.
New services include Flibco's route linking Stansted with Enfield, Wood Green and Finsbury Park, while Arriva has enhanced its 723 service between Stansted and Harlow, reducing journey times and improving access for passengers and airport staff.
More than a third of airport employees, around 5,000 people, now travel to work by public transport. This is supported by investment in bus services, cycling facilities and other sustainable travel initiatives across the airport campus.
Looking ahead, work is progressing on plans for a major redevelopment of Stansted's bus and coach station, with proposals including increased capacity, improved waiting areas, better passenger information and enhanced ticketing facilities.
The forum also received an update on East West Rail, the major project linking Oxford, Milton Keynes, Bedford and Cambridge.
The new railway is expected to strengthen connections between Stansted and some of the UK's fastest-growing centres for science, technology and innovation, providing further opportunities for passengers to travel by rail.
John Pope, Chair of the Stansted Airport Transport Forum, said:
"The past year has seen real progress across our transport network, with growing numbers of passengers and employees choosing sustainable ways to travel to and from the airport.
"Reaching almost 14 million passengers travelling by public transport in a year is a significant milestone, particularly as we celebrate 25 years of the Stansted Airport Transport Forum.
"It reflects the strong partnerships that have helped improve rail, bus and coach connections to the airport over the past quarter of a century.
"From the successful trial of 24-hour Stansted Express services and improvements to local bus routes, to plans for a major redevelopment of the airport's bus and coach station, we're continuing to improve the range of travel options available to passengers and staff while supporting the airport's sustainable growth.
"The forum plays an important role in bringing together transport operators, local authorities, businesses and community organisations, and we look forward to building on this progress and delivering further improvements in the years ahead."
The Stansted Airport Transport Forum took place at the Radisson Blu Hotel on November 11.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: London Stansted records busiest ever day as transformation programme continues to progress
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
London Stansted's growing importance to the capital and wider East of England was reflected in a record October that saw nearly 2.8m passengers use its terminal.
Stansted also continued to make progress on its major investment programme, which will signal a further phase of growth over the next 20 years.
The airport welcomed 2.79m passengers during October, up 4.2% on 2025 and 113,000 more than its previous record for the month.
That included its busiest day on record - Sunday 25 October - when 109,881 passengers travelled through the airport.
Growth was driven by a strong October half-term and the popularity of flagship routes, including its direct services to Istanbul, which not only connect to the Turkish capital but onwards to more than 350 global destinations. More than 101,000 people flew to and from Istanbul for business or leisure during the month.
Stansted's unrivalled European network also drove growth, with Dublin and Edinburgh the second and third most flown to destinations. Spain was the most popular individual country, with 462,000 people travelling there, followed by Italy and Turkey.
The record October performance comes as London Stansted continues to make good progress on its transformation programme, which is designed to increase capacity, enhance operational resilience and further improve the passenger experience.
Progress was showcased during a recent visit by the Secretary of State for Transport, Heidi Alexander MP, who toured the airport and viewed work on the new skylink walkways that are key to extending the existing terminal building and unlocking future growth.
The Secretary of State saw how the project was progressing with foundation and steelworks underway while the skylinks are pre-assembly ‘offsite’ in a vacant airport hangar before they are transported across to the construction site in the coming months.
Gareth Powell, London Stansted's Managing Director, said:
"This was another landmark month for London Stansted, culminating in our busiest ever day and busiest October on record.
“The record passenger numbers reflect both the continuing strength of demand across our network and the busy half-term holiday getaway, which saw thousands of passengers, including overseas visitors to the UK, choose Stansted for autumn breaks and visits to friends and family.
“The airport now serves nearly 31m passengers a year and plays a key role in driving trade, investment and tourism for London and the East of England. With planning permission to serve up to 51m passengers over the next two decades, with provides us with a strong platform to unlock the spare capacity on our existing runway and deliver our ambitious plans to increase passenger numbers and help improve the UK’s connectivity with the rest of the world.
“In addition, we're also making good progress on our transformation programme. It was a pleasure last week to welcome the Secretary of State for Transport to the airport and demonstrate the scale of our investment, the progress being made to support future growth and enhancements to the airport experience for passengers in the years ahead.
"As this work continues to ramp up, we remain focused on delivering an efficient and reliable experience for every passenger flying from London Stansted while continuing to further develop our route network to support connectivity, trade and economic growth across our region."

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: 25 years of shaping transport links and connectivity
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
London Stansted will next week mark 25 years of working with transport operators, local authorities and community partners to help make it one of the UK's best connected airports for public transport.
The milestone will be celebrated at the annual Stansted Area Transport Forum, which has helped shape the airport's transport network and drive increased use of public transport by passengers and colleagues since it was established.
Over the past 25 years, passenger numbers at Stansted have grown from nine million a year to more than 30 million, while public transport use has risen from around a third of passengers to almost half.
Today, more than 14 million passengers travel to and from the airport by train, bus or coach each year.
The growth has been supported by major improvements to rail, coach and bus services, helping Stansted become the major UK airport with the highest public transport mode share.
The forum brings together transport operators, local authorities, businesses and community groups to discuss how people travel to and from the airport and identify opportunities to improve connections across the region.
This year's event will look back at some of the biggest transport developments of the past 25 years, including the expansion of the Stansted Express, growth of the airport's coach network, investment in cycling and walking routes, and schemes helping airport employees travel more sustainably.
It will also explore how public transport can support the airport's future growth while reducing congestion and emissions.
Steve Mills, Surface Access Strategy Manager at London Stansted, said:
“The way people travel to and from London Stansted has changed enormously over the past 25 years. We've seen passenger numbers more than triple, while public transport has become the first choice for millions of people travelling through the airport every year. That progress has only been possible because transport operators, local authorities and local communities have worked together to improve connections and give people more travel options. As we look ahead, continuing to invest in sustainable transport will be essential if we are to support future growth and remain one of the best-connected airports in the UK.”
Recent priorities for the forum have included trials of 24-hour Stansted Express services, new coach and bus links, improved rail connectivity and plans for future investment in the airport's transport infrastructure.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: The Secretary of State for Transport visits to see transformation progress
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
London Stansted this week welcomed The Secretary of State for Transport Heidi Alexander MP, who saw first-hand how the airport's transformation programme will boost the role it plays driving trade, investment and tourism for London and the East of England.
During the visit the Secretary of State toured the airport’s recently enlarged security hall that features 17 latest technology scanners that allows passengers to leave liquids and large electrical items in hand luggage, as well as receiving an update on the construction of airport’s new skylink walkways.
Stansted has welcomed a record-breaking number of passengers this year, and saw it achieve its busiest ever flying day this summer with over 700 aircraft movements, and the Secretary of State got to see first-hand during an airfield tour how the airport successfully delivers an efficient, reliable and safe flight operation every day.
The visit concluded at the airport’s new on-site solar farm, the only one of its kind at a London airport, which became operation in September this year and is now helping power the airport and supports Stansted’s commitment to achieve net zero carbon emissions from its direct airport operations by no later than 2038.
The skylinks are one of the first features to be delivered as part of a wider, five-year programme that will help the airport increase passenger volumes up to 51m over the next two decades without the need for a new runway.
This development will see Stansted build on the economic contribution it already delivers to the UK, with latest figures from York Aviation revealing it supports £11.3bn of Gross Value Added each year, through a combination of direct jobs and by stimulating trade and tourism.
Gareth Powell, London Stansted’s Managing Director, said:
“We were delighted to welcome the Secretary of State to London Stansted and join us to see first-hand the progress we are making in delivering our ambitious investment plans to create an airport ready for the future and offer an even greater choice of destinations for our passengers.
“This year has been a very exciting period for everyone connected with London Stansted as we continue to welcome a record number of passengers, new airlines and routes and drive forward the airport’s transformation programme, so today’s visit was a fantastic chance to showcase the real momentum we have behind our vision for London Stansted.
“As one of the UK’s busiest airports serving more than 30m passengers a year, London Stansted already plays a key role in providing international connectivity for London and the East of England, offering 200 destinations across 40 countries, and more scheduled connections to Europe than any other UK airport.
“World-leading carriers Emirates and Turkish Airlines also connect passengers to hundreds of global destinations via their hubs in Dubai and Istanbul and act as a gateway to the world for our region.
“Last year we secured planning permission to serve up to 51m passengers a year, which alongside our investment plans, provides us with a strong platform to unlock the spare capacity on our existing runway and deliver our ambitious plans to sustainably increase passenger numbers, support economic growth and make a significant contribution to improving the UK’s connectivity with the rest of the world.”
Heidi Alexander, Transport Secretary, said:
“We support airport expansion where it balances economic growth with climate, noise and air quality obligations. I'm pleased to see Stansted’s plans to grow passenger numbers responsibly – boosting connectivity, jobs and growth across the East of England, while meeting environmental commitments.
“Stansted’s new solar farm is a shining example of how airports can cut their carbon footprint and reduce emissions as they grow. This comes as we invest £43 million to boost innovation that makes the sector even greener.”
The five-year transformation programme will deliver wide-ranging benefits to passengers and help secure links to ev

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Cyprus Airways to launch daily Stansted-Larnaca flights
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
London Stansted is set to gain a new daily link to Cyprus after Cyprus Airways announced plans to launch flights to Larnaca next spring.
The Larnaca-based airline will begin operating the year-round service on 23 April 2027, offering daily flights between Stansted and the popular Mediterranean destination.
The new route will provide greater choice for holidaymakers, business travellers and people visiting friends and family, while strengthening links between the UK and Cyprus.
London Stansted's Aviation Director, Simon Gorrighan, welcomed the announcement. He said:
“We're delighted to welcome Cyprus Airways to London Stansted and add even more choice for passengers travelling between the UK and Cyprus.
"Larnaca is already a very popular destination, so a new daily service is fantastic news for passengers across our region.
"We look forward to welcoming Cyprus Airways to Stansted next April and working with the airline as it develops its operation at the airport.”
Thanos Pascalis, chief executive of Cyprus Airways, said the UK remained one of the airline's most important markets. He said:
"The launch of our new service to London Stansted is an important addition to the Cyprus Airways network and reflects our continued focus on strengthening connectivity between Cyprus and the United Kingdom.
"The United Kingdom is a particularly important market for Cyprus, with strong demand across leisure, business and visiting friends and relatives.
"By adding London Stansted to our network from April 2027, we are providing our customers with greater choice and flexibility while further strengthening our presence in one of Cyprus' most significant international markets.
“We look forward to welcoming passengers on board and offering them the convenience, reliability and authentic Cypriot hospitality that define Cyprus Airways.”
The Stansted route forms part of Cyprus Airways' wider expansion plans. The airline is also launching new services from Larnaca to Rome and Munich in December 2026.
Cyprus Airways operates a fleet of Airbus A320 and A220 aircraft from its base at Larnaca International Airport and flies to destinations including Paris, Milan, Athens, Heraklion, Tel Aviv, Beirut and Dubai.
Flights are available to book through the Cyprus Airways website at Cyprus Airways .

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Josh Dean MP visits academy that has helped more than 3,500 people find work and explore careers
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Josh Dean, MP for Hertford and Bishop's Stortford, has visited Stansted Airport's Employment and Skills Academy to learn more about its work supporting local people into training and employment.
More than 3,500 people have received free careers support through the Academy, which helps jobseekers build skills, gain confidence and access opportunities across the airport community.
The Academy works with more than 200 businesses based at London Stansted, supporting people looking to start work, return to employment or change careers. Opportunities span a wide range of sectors, including hospitality, retail, security, logistics and aviation.
A total of 330 people completed training through the Academy during the last financial year, benefiting from CV workshops, interview preparation, careers advice and industry-focused training courses designed to help them move into employment.
Josh Dean MP said:
"Visiting the Stansted Airport's Employment and Skills Academy was a real pleasure, and we are so fortunate to have such a fantastic training and education facility right on our doorstep. With around a one million people currently not in education, employment or training, investing in technical skills and vocational education has never been more important. The Academy is helping to meet this challenge, while also supporting people of all ages to develop new skills.
“Whether they're taking their first steps into work or looking to retrain for a new career, the Academy is opening doors for people across our community and helping them gain the skills and confidence they need for the future. It was inspiring to hear directly from students about their experiences and the opportunities their courses are creating for them, and I am looking forward to visiting again in the future.”
In addition to skills training, the Academy works closely with job centres and local authorities to widen access to employment opportunities. Recent initiatives have included a mentoring programme for young people not in education, employment or training (NEET), helping them build confidence, develop workplace skills and explore career options at the airport.
Having previously attended the Academy, Wendy Reynolds now works as a MAG Landside Receptionist at the airport. She said:
“The course genuinely gave me 100% confidence; thanks to the positive feedback I received throughout. While completing the course, I applied for the Landside Receptionist position. My interview took place shortly after the course ended, and I’m pleased to say I was successful and offered the job.”
Nathan Mullane, the airport’s Employment and Skills Manager, said:
"Starting a new job or changing direction can feel quite daunting, so it's great to be able to help people build their confidence and take that next step. Seeing so many local people go on to find work and start new careers through the Academy is something we're really proud of."

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Cambridgeshire and the East of England helping power economic success
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Cambridgeshire and the wider East of England are critical economic drivers for the UK, with growth powered by international, knowledge-intensive industries, new data reveals.
Exclusive analysis released by London Stansted reveals services exports in the Cambridgeshire County Council area grew by 152% between 2016 and 2023, faster than it did in any major region of the UK, including London (101%). The average for England as a whole was 75%.
The analysis, produced for London Stansted by WPI Economics, also highlights 62% of total trade in services in Cambridgeshire CC involved partners from outside of the EU.
This was again higher than any major region in England, including London (61%) and the wider East of England (60%).
The data also reveals the wider East of England continues to go from strength to strength with international services trade in the region growing by 96% between 2016 and 2023. Growth was particularly strong beyond the EU, where services trade increased by 112%.
The findings were released as 600 leaders from across research, industry, investment, government and the wider innovation ecosystem gathered at the at the Innovate Cambridge Summit 2026 at the Guildhall, Cambridge, to explore the next phase of innovation-led growth for Cambridge and the UK.
London Stansted plays a key role in providing international connectivity for the region, serving 200 destinations across 40 countries, and offering more scheduled connections to Europe than any other UK airport.
World-leading carriers Emirates and Turkish Airlines also connect passengers to hundreds of global destinations via their hubs in Dubai and Istanbul and act as a gateway to the world for the East of England.
Gareth Powell, London Stansted’s Managing Director, said:
"It’s been very clear for a long time that Cambridge and the wider East of England play vital roles in the economic success of the UK, and this new data clearly underlines the truly global nature of the region’s economic growth and the importance of the UK’s international trading relationships.
“The research shows Cambridge is the country's global services superpower and the region’s star performer with its world-leading innovation economy thriving on global connectivity.
“London Stansted is a key enabler of this economic growth, supporting the region in attracting world-leading businesses in technology, life sciences, advanced manufacturing and research.
“London Stansted already serves more European destinations than any other airport in the UK, and key airline partners such as Emirates and Turkish Airlines provide up to 350 onward connections across the globe via their world-leading hubs in Dubai and Istanbul.
“This research shows international connectivity is fundamental to economic success, and we expect to play an even greater role supporting the growth of the region through our investment plans to expand our capacity.
“Our transformation programme is about creating an airport ready for the future, attracting new airlines and serving even more routes. We’re confident this investment and vision will help sustain on-going economic success and power the future ambitions of Cambridge and the East of England.”
Previous WPI Economics research, called Services Superpower , found that services are central to the UK’s economic strength, with fast-growing sectors such as fintech and life sciences relying on international connectivity to trade, attract investment and drive growth.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Jet2 extends Tunisia flights into winter
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Jet2 is extending its new Tunisia programme from London Stansted into winter 2027/28 following strong demand for the destination.
Flights to Enfidha-Hammamet International Airport, which are due to launch for summer 2027, will now continue until November 28, rather than ending on October 31.
The twice-weekly Wednesday and Sunday service will then restart on February 13, 2028, before continuing through the summer.
The extended season means passengers will be able to fly from Stansted to Tunisia during both the October and February half-term holidays.
Jet2 announced Tunisia as a new destination from the airport in June, with flights and holidays going on sale for summer 2027.
The airline says strong early demand has led it to extend the season.
Steve Heapy, CEO of Jet2, said:
“The response to the launch of Tunisia for Summer 2027 has been fantastic. With plenty of demand from customers and independent travel agents looking to book early and looking to book Tunisia for some winter sunshine, we are delighted to be extending our programme from London Stansted Airport.
“This expansion gives customers across the South East even more opportunities to enjoy everything that Tunisia has to offer, whilst enjoying our industry-leading customer service. We know there is enormous appetite for this destination, and we are pleased to be responding by offering customers greater choice and flexibility when planning their holidays.”
Ciaran Brannigan, Commercial Director at London Stansted, said:
“It’s great news for passengers across the London Stansted region that Jet2 is to extend its popular summer 27 schedule to Tunisia into the winter season. The extra flights will provide even more choice and reflects the strong demand from holidaymakers to enjoy a winter sunshine break from their local airport.”
For more information, visit Jet2.com or Jet2holidays.com.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Transformation brings new jobs into focus at careers fair
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Companies helping deliver London Stansted’s transformation project were among 30 employers meeting almost 1,800 jobseekers at the airport’s latest careers fair.
Construction firms Farrans and Laing O’Rourke attended the event, giving visitors the chance to find out about careers being created as work at the airport gathers pace.
They spoke to jobseekers about the projects they are delivering, the types of roles available and the skills needed to join their teams.
The fair, held at the Radisson Blu Hotel at London Stansted, brought together employers including DHL, Ryanair, UPS, Jet2, Mulberry and MAG Stansted, offering opportunities across aviation, customer service, retail, hospitality, logistics and engineering.
Nathan Mullane, the airport’s Employment and Skills Manager, said:
“It was fantastic to see so many people coming along to find out about the opportunities available at London Stansted. There’s a lot happening at the airport, and our transformation isn’t just about improving Stansted for passengers. It’s also creating opportunities for local people to build careers and develop new skills.
“Having companies delivering some of our biggest projects at the careers fair meant people could speak directly to them, hear about the work they’re doing and find out what opportunities are available. We want local people to benefit from the investment being made at Stansted and hopefully some of those who came along will go on to play a part in the airport’s future.”
Farrans is working on the construction of the airport’s new Skylink walkways, which will connect the terminal and the satellite buildings housing the departure and arrival gates.
The centrepiece of Stansted’s transformation is a three-bay extension to the existing terminal, adding 16,500m² of space and creating a brighter, more spacious environment with new shops, bars and restaurants.
Eddie Burton, Stakeholder and Social Value Manager at Farrans, said:
“We were really pleased to be part of this careers fair which gave us the chance to engage with local businesses as well as meet people interested in finding out more about the work we’re doing at London Stansted Airport. We’re currently recruiting for people to join our graduate and apprenticeship programmes with excellent opportunities for early careers candidates and more senior construction roles. Our award-winning graduate programme will have two intakes in 2027 beginning in June and September and applications are open now on our website.”

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: 1,300 passengers and staff learn lifesaving CPR skills
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
More than 1,300 passengers and airport colleagues learned potentially lifesaving CPR skills at London Stansted as part of Restart a Heart Day.
A team from Essex & Herts Air Ambulance spent Friday, October 16, at the airport showing passengers heading off on their holidays and airport staff how to perform CPR and use a defibrillator.
The event was held as part of Restart a Heart Day, a national initiative encouraging more people to learn CPR and giving them the confidence to act if someone suffers a cardiac arrest.
Around 40,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests happen in the UK each year, with survival rates below 10%. Essex & Herts Air Ambulance attended 570 cardiac arrests last year.
Adam Carr, Critical Care Paramedic at Essex & Herts Air Ambulance, who leads the charity’s CPR Smart programme, said:
“CPR isn’t hard, but people need to know the basics. It was brilliant to have so many willing volunteers looking to refresh their skills. If any one of those people is now on the scene when someone has a cardiac arrest, they can intervene and make a life-saving difference. CPR is something we all need to be able to do.”
Natalie Putt, Head of Customer Operations at London Stansted, said:
“It was great to welcome Essex & Herts Air Ambulance back to Stansted for Restart a Heart Day. You never know when you might need to use CPR, and having the confidence to step in could save someone’s life. Our customer service teams are trained as first responders, but these are simple skills that anyone can learn, which is why days like this are so valuable.”
More information about Essex & Herts Air Ambulance and its work is available at ehaat.org , while CPR advice is available on its life-saving first aid page .

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Six spooky half-term getaways for Halloween
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
From Dracula’s Transylvania to Edinburgh’s underground vaults, there are plenty of places to get into the Halloween spirit this October half-term, with direct flights from London Stansted to six destinations offering ghost tours, haunted attractions and seasonal events.
More than 860,000 passengers are expected to travel through London Stansted during the October half-term, which culminates in Halloween on Saturday, October 31.
Edinburgh, Transylvania, Prague, Amsterdam, Copenhagen and Budapest all offer plenty of opportunities for a spooky autumn getaway.
With more European destinations than any other UK airport, London Stansted offers plenty of choice for those looking to get away this half-term.
Edinburgh is one of the closest options, with direct flights from Stansted with easyJet and Ryanair. The Scottish capital’s historic Old Town is the perfect setting for ghost tours through its winding streets and underground vaults, while the Edinburgh Dungeon offers a more theatrical take on the city’s darker history.
Transylvania is a must for anyone drawn to the legends of Dracula. Flights from Stansted operate to Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca, providing access to the region and Bran Castle, one of the landmarks most closely associated with the famous vampire. Its Halloween programme runs from October 24 to November 1.
Prague offers a suitably spooky backdrop, with its cobbled streets, Gothic architecture and ghost tours through the historic Old Town. Just outside the city, visitors can also explore the Sedlec Ossuary in Kutná Hora, better known as the Bone Church for its striking interior decorated with human bones. Ryanair operates daily flights from Stansted to Prague.
Amsterdam has Halloween events around the city, as well as the Amsterdam Dungeon, where visitors can delve into the darker side of the city’s history. Its famous canals, museums and other attractions also make it a great choice for a half-term break. easyJet operates daily flights from Stansted to Amsterdam.
Copenhagen gets into the Halloween spirit at Tivoli Gardens, where pumpkins, seasonal displays and entertainment transform the famous amusement park during October. Ryanair operates daily flights from Stansted to Copenhagen.
Budapest offers ghost and vampire-themed walking tours around its historic Castle District. For a change of pace, visitors can relax in the city’s famous thermal baths or explore the sights along the Danube. Ryanair operates daily flights from Stansted to Budapest.
Neringa Ohrstrom, Head of Brand and Marketing at London Stansted, said:
“With October half-term leading straight into Halloween this year, it’s a great opportunity to swap trick-or-treating at home for a short break somewhere a little different. From ghost tours and Dracula legends to Halloween events and historic attractions, there are some fantastic places to explore, all within reach with direct flights from Stansted.”
For more information on destinations available from London Stansted, visit stanstedairport.com .

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Ed Richardson: London needs investment at Stansted to keep growing and competing globally
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
We're delighted to launch our new guest blog series, where we hear from different organisations about the importance of international connectivity.
First up is Edward Richardson, Programme Director, Transport at BusinessLDN who reflects on the powerful role London Stansted has to play providing easy and convenient access to the world for the capital .
As the capital of an island trading nation, London’s success has always been built on its ability to connect with the rest of the world. For businesses, investors, visitors and workers, our international connectivity is not a luxury – it is a fundamental part of what makes London one of the world’s leading cities.
Aviation is central to that success. It enables trade and tourism, connects businesses with customers and markets, and opens up opportunities for Londoners to work and build careers in a diverse and growing sector.
That is why new investment at London Stansted matters.
Today, Stansted welcomes more than 30 million passengers a year and connects London and the wider UK to more than 200 destinations. It offers the largest number of direct European routes of any UK airport and handles more than £12 billion of trade value each year.
For London businesses, that connectivity matters. Whether it is a company looking to reach customers in Europe, an international visitor coming to the capital, or a business relying on global supply chains, the ability to move people and goods efficiently is an important part of our economic infrastructure.
Which is why it’s positive that Stansted is investing for the future.
BusinessLDN’s recent Pathway to Delivery: Expanding London’s Global Connections, produced with Arcadis, highlights the scale of the opportunity when it comes to improving the UK’s international links. Across London’s major global gateways, more than £53.5 billion of private investment is in the pipeline, including £1.1 billion at London Stansted.
At Stansted, that investment is focused on expanding its existing terminal by 40%, improving passenger facilities and making better use of the airport’s existing runway. Planning permission has also been granted to increase the airport’s passenger capacity from 43 million to 51 million a year by 2040, without increasing the number of flights the airport is permitted to operate.
This is about more than passengers. It is about jobs, skills, investment and opportunity.
Stansted is already the largest single-site employer in the East of England, with more than 12,000 people working across around 200 businesses on the airport campus. And its role in developing the next generation of talent is equally important.
Stansted Airport College has trained more than 2,500 students since opening in 2018, offering specialist courses in aviation, engineering, aircraft maintenance, logistics, travel and tourism. Its students include young people travelling from across the wider London and Essex area to access specialist training and a direct pathway into the aviation industry.
The college is now looking to expand significantly, with plans to increase capacity from 568 to around 1,350 students. That is a powerful example of how investment in aviation infrastructure can also be an investment in people and skills.
For London, the message is clear: if we want a capital that continues to trade, attract investment, welcome visitors and compete internationally, we need the infrastructure to connect it to the world.
Stansted is an important part of that infrastructure. Its investment plans offer an opportunity to strengthen London’s connectivity while creating jobs, developing skills and supporting growth across the capital and the wider region.
The task now is to make sure that the policy, planning, skills and transport connections are in place to turn that investment ambition into reality.
London’s future growth will depend on many things. But one of them is certain: we cannot afford to take our global connections for granted.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Late summer sun drives record-breaking September at London Stansted
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
Strong demand for late summer sun and long weekend breaks helped London Stansted welcome a record-breaking 2.88m passengers in September.
The record monthly total was an increase of 6.4% on the same month last year and beat the previous record for September - set in 2024 - by 170,000 passengers.
The top sunshine destinations during the month were Palma de Mallorca, Alicante, Faro and Malaga with Dublin, Istanbul, Barcelona and Rome some of the most in-demand short break and city destinations.
The most popular countries across August were Spain, Italy, and Turkey.
Stansted recorded 12 days in the month when passenger numbers topped 100,000, having never previously exceeded that number during September.
The airport’s rolling 12-month passenger total now stands at 30.87m, up 2.9% on 2025.
The month also saw Stansted’s transformation programme pass two significant milestones, including the 12.8MW on-site solar farm becoming operational to begin helping power the airport.
In addition, the airside passenger bussing facility and link bridge were both successfully removed, clearing the way for foundation works to begin for the new terminal extension, marking the move from the demolition to the construction phase of the project.
Gareth Powell, London Stansted’s Managing Director, said:
“Following our busiest ever summer season, we saw no let up during September as the strong demand continued as we once again welcomed record breaking numbers of passengers to the airport, all taking advantage of the choice, value and reliable service we offer at London Stansted.
“The continued growth in passenger numbers highlights the vital role we play in connecting people, businesses and communities across our region with destinations across Europe and beyond.
“Alongside this growth, we are continuing to make good progress with our transformation programme which is designed to deliver an even better passenger experience while supporting our long-term sustainability ambitions.
“I’m delighted our new solar farm is now up and running and helping power the airport, while we have now completed key enabling works for the terminal extension which moves this project to its next phase.
“Our focus now turns to preparing for the half-term holidays, which we expect to be another busy period for the airport, so our teams will be working hard to deliver the best possible experience for every passenger choosing to fly from London Stansted.”

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: New wildlife haven created for bees and butterflies
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
A new wildlife haven the size of four football pitches has been created at London Stansted, giving bees, butterflies and other wildlife a place to feed, nest and thrive.
The 3.18-hectare site near Bury Lodge Lane, close to the M11, provides a range of new habitats for wildlife. Species already recorded at the site include the patchwork leaf-cutter bee, large-headed resin bee and cinnabar moth caterpillar, alongside wildflowers such as bird's-foot trefoil, oxeye daisy and Queen Anne's lace.
The restored grassland includes log piles, bee posts, earth banks and shallow scrapes, creating places for insects and other wildlife to feed, nest and shelter. Wildlife began using some of the new features almost immediately.
A new footpath from the Long Stay car park is also being created, providing improved access to the area.
The project is among a number of environmental initiatives highlighted in London Stansted's latest Sustainability Report, published this week, and forms part of the airport's Biodiversity Net Gain commitments linked to its wider transformation programme.
Joshua Stafford, Ecology and Biodiversity Lead at London Stansted, said:
“This project shows how relatively small changes can make a real difference for wildlife. Features such as bee posts, log piles and earth banks provide valuable places for pollinating insects to nest and shelter, and wildlife began using them almost immediately. By combining long-term grassland restoration with these additional features, we're creating a richer and more varied habitat that will support nature and biodiversity for decades to come.”
The habitat scheme builds on other biodiversity initiatives across the airport, including the management of a wildlife area north of the runway, support for rare oxlip flower rewilding projects with the National Trust, and London Stansted's membership of the Essex Wildlife Trust Investor in Wildlife Scheme.
The airport's latest Sustainability Report highlights progress across a range of environmental, community and economic initiatives, including work to enhance biodiversity and create new habitats across the airport site. Full report is available here.

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Aerozone celebrates 30,000 visitors as Priti Patel joins milestone event
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
More than 30,000 students have now visited London Stansted's Aerozone education centre since it opened in 2015, marking a major milestone for the airport's long-running programme to inspire young people and introduce them to careers in aviation.
The achievement was celebrated during a visit by 20 Year 10 students from Lift New Rickstones Academy in Witham, who spent the day taking part in hands-on activities designed to showcase the world of aviation and the wide range of jobs that help keep an airport running.
The milestone event was attended by Witham MP Priti Patel, who met students and learned more about Aerozone's work with schools and community groups across the East of England.
Based at the airport, Aerozone gives young people the chance to explore careers in aviation through interactive activities linked to science, technology, engineering and maths (STEM).
Students can meet airport colleagues, learn about the different roles that exist across the aviation sector and gain a better understanding of how an international airport operates.
Since opening in 2015, Aerozone has hosted more than 950 visits from 259 schools and educational groups from across Essex, East London, Hertfordshire, Suffolk and the wider East of England.
Witham MP Priti Patel said:
“Reaching 30,000 visitors is a fantastic milestone for Aerozone and a real testament to the work being done at Stansted to inspire young people and open their eyes to the opportunities available in aviation. It was great to meet students from the Lift New Rickstones and see how Aerozone brings careers to life by giving young people practical experience and the chance to meet those working across the airport.
“We need to be doing everything we can to equip our young people with the skills, confidence, and ambition to succeed, particularly in sectors like aviation, engineering, and STEM where there are so many exciting career opportunities. I know how important Stansted is to our region and our local economy, and initiatives like Aerozone are helping to build the skilled workforce of the future. My congratulations go to everyone involved in reaching this milestone.”
Alex Smith, Education Manager at London Stansted, said:
“It's amazing to think that more than 30,000 people have now come through Aerozone. We see students arrive not really knowing what happens at an airport and leave excited about careers they never knew existed. If we can open their eyes to the opportunities available and get them thinking differently about what they might want to do in the future, then that's a real success for us.”
As well as Aerozone, the airport supports a number of education and skills programmes, including the Stansted Airport Employment and Skills Academy and Stansted Airport College, helping people of all ages develop skills and explore careers in aviation.
Marcella M'Rabety, Head of Social Sustainability at MAG, said:
"Aerozone is often where a young person's interest in aviation begins. We're really proud to have reached this milestone, and we’re looking forward to doing much more. We want to build on this work by giving more primary and secondary school students the chance to meet employers, develop their skills and see the opportunities available to them. Creating opportunities and inspiring future talent is an important part of the role we play in our local communities."

https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.title: Flight path to a new career at jobs fair
https://mediacentre.stanstedairport.com/.text:
More than 500 jobs will be on offer when London Stansted hosts a careers fair next month.
The free event, taking place at the Radisson Blu Hotel on Thursday, October 15, will bring together 25 employers from across the airport, giving jobseekers the chance to explore vacancies, meet recruiters and find out more about careers at Stansted.
Employers attending include DHL, Ryanair, UPS, Jet2, Mulberry and MAG Stansted, with jobs available across aviation, customer service, retail, hospitality, logistics and engineering.
Visitors will also be able to learn more about opportunities linked to the airport's transformation programme, with construction firms Laing O'Rourke and Farrans hosting dedicated stands.
The event is being organised by London Stansted's Employment and Skills Academy and will also offer advice on skills, training and qualifications.
Jennifer Crossling, Senior Education and Employment Manager at London Stansted, said:
“With more than 500 jobs on offer, this is a great opportunity for people to see what's available and meet employers face-to-face. Whether you're looking for your first job, a career change or a fresh start, we'd encourage you to come along and find out more.”
London Stansted is the East of England's largest single-site employer, supporting more than 12,000 jobs across around 200 businesses based at the airport.
The jobs fair will take place from 10am to 2pm and is free to attend. Anyone interested in attending can register at: London Stansted Airport Jobs Fair – Eventbrite

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Harwich Haven Authority appoints Clive Quantrill as Non-Executive Director
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
Harwich Haven Authority has appointed Clive Quantrill as a Non-Executive Director, effective from 1 January 2027, following a robust recruitment process.
Clive brings more than 15 years of board-level experience in large, complex and regulated organisations, alongside significant expertise in strategy, transformation, governance, financial oversight and risk management.
During his career with BT, Clive held a range of senior strategy, transformation and commercial leadership positions, most recently serving as Director of Transformation for BT’s business customers. He currently works part-time as a Senior Partner at Cambridge Management Consulting, advising UK and international clients on strategy and organisational change.
Clive also holds a number of Non-Executive Director positions. He is a Board member of the Independent Office for Police Conduct, where he chairs the Audit and Risk Assurance Committee, a Non-Executive Director of the Valuation Tribunal Service and a Director of Paradigm Trust, a multi-academy schools trust.
Based in Suffolk, Clive has longstanding connections to the waterways and communities of the region. He lives in Waldringfield on the River Deben and is a lifelong sailor of the Deben and Orwell, with family ties to the maritime trades of the River Stour. His understanding of the Haven’s importance to the regional economy and the UK’s wider supply chain brings valuable local insight to the role.
Clive said:
“I’m delighted to be joining Harwich Haven Authority. Having lived locally for many years, I know how important the Haven is to the communities around it and to the UK’s supply chain. I believe strongly in the trust port model, which reinvests for the long-term benefit of customers, communities and the environment, and I look forward to supporting the Board in continuing that success.”
The appointment coincides with Nicola Hancock completing her second term as a Non-Executive Director and leaving the Authority at the end of 2026. Harwich Haven Authority thanks Nicola for her contribution and commitment during her time on the Board.
In making Non-Executive Director appointments, the Board considers the combination of skills, experience and perspectives required across the Board as a whole. Clive’s appointment further strengthens this collective expertise and supports the Authority’s continued focus on balancing strong commercial performance with its responsibilities as a trust port, reinvesting for the long-term benefit of customers, communities and the environment.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: 2026-06: Information required for Non-Routine Towage Operations
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
All non-routine towage operations taking place in Harwich Haven Authority’s jurisdiction are subject to an assessment process and require Harbour Master approval. The Tug Master or Towage Vessel Operator must submit a completed Non-Routine Towage application form and supporting documentation a minimum of 2 working days prior to the intended date of the towage operation or as soon as practicable.
Non-routine towage is defined as any commercial towage operation that is not routine ship assist towage provided by tugs which have been assessed by the Authority as fit for purpose. It includes the towing of a vessel, structure, or floating object where the operation involves unusual hazards, abnormal circumstances, environmental risks, specialist planning, or operational complexities.
If in any doubt, it is advisable to complete a non-routine towage application to avoid any delays in acceptance or contact the Harbour Master’s office (+44 (0) 1255 243030).
Submitted non-routine towage applications will be reviewed by the Harbour Master to determine the suitability of the proposed towage plan, the pilot and escort vessel requirements and if a pre-planning meeting is required prior to approval.
In the event of any subsequent changes to an approved non-routine towage operation, a further 2 working days ’ notice will be required to review and amend the approved plan.
This notice replaces Port Information Notice No. 02 of 2018, which is now withdrawn.

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Pioneering Project Launched on the Blackwater Estuary to Restore Saltmarsh Habitat and Support Coastal Resilience
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A new initiative will see sediment dredged from Harwich Haven Authority’s routine harbour maintenance dredging reused to restore shingle beach nesting habitat for endangered seabirds, including the amber-listed Little Tern. BUDS (Beneficial Use of Dredged Sediment) in the Blackwater Estuary will see the RSPB, Harwich Haven Authority, Essex Wildlife Trust and ZSL, alongside local conservationists, working together to protect the diverse and internationally important coastal habitat found on the east coast of England, whilst reducing flood risk for homes and businesses
Beginning in October 2026, the £2.5m project (funded by the EA/Defra Natural Flood Management programme and the Transforming the Thames project, led by the Zoological Society of London (ZSL)), funded by the Endangered Landscapes & Seascapes Programme, managed by the Cambridge Conservation Initiative in partnership with Arcadia) will reduce coastal erosion and flood risk in the Blackwater Estuary.
The project will be delivered in partnership with Harwich Haven Authority, one of the UK’s largest trust ports, using dredged sediment from harbour maintenance to recharge the foreshore at several locations. The beach recharge will protect the eroding foreshore including important saltmarsh and mudflat and reduce pressure on aging coastal flood defences, whilst also creating nesting habitat for beach nesting bird species including amber-listed Little Tern, Ringed Plover and Oystercatcher.
The project makes use of clean dredged sand (that would otherwise be disposed of at sea) for beneficial purposes. Less than 1% of dredged sediment is currently used for beneficial purposes nationally, despite the significant benefit such projects can deliver for nature and society including habitat restoration, natural flood management and carbon sequestration.
Beach recharge is the process of using dredged sand and shingle to top up beaches and increase flood protection and nesting habitat. The beach recharge on the Blackwater Estuary will build on work delivered by the Mersea Harbour Protection Trust, a charitable trust set up by a group of local individuals in 2022. Once deposited, it is expected that the sediment will respond to the tides and reform into a more natural shape, further protecting the sheltered creeks and channels of West Mersea from large waves and storm surges that can enter the estuary. This will help to ensure West Mersea’s future as an important commercial boating and fishing centre and native oyster fishery.
During spring and summer, restored shingle banks will provide a place for ground-nesting birds such as Little Tern, Common Tern and Ringed Plover to raise their young.  These species are particularly susceptible to recreational disturbance as well as rising sea levels, nesting in shallow scrapes just above the tide line, so providing new nesting areas is crucial. It is hoped that the new areas of recharge will gradually colonise with stress-tolerant plants including sea kale and yellow horned poppy as well as rare invertebrate communities.
The beaches will also protect important saltmarsh that helps absorb wave energy, helping to limit flood water levels inland and reduce the extent of coastal flooding.
Saltmarsh is a rare and special habitat in the UK that teems with wildlife, but much has been lost through past land claim for agriculture, while it is also under threat from climate change-driven sea level rise.  In time, the restored saltmarsh will repopulate with native salt-tolerant plants Common Sea Heather,-Lavender and Samphire that help to catch more mud and silt, continually growing and expanding this special habitat.
Work will also benefit many species of bird, some of which are threatened, by providing habitat rich food for overwintering wading birds including Black-tailed Godwits, Redshank, Curlews, Grey Plovers, Knot and Dunlin. https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Fab five celebrate 180 years at Harwich Haven Authority
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
A group of colleagues are celebrating an incredible 180 years of service to one of the UK’s busiest and most important ports.
The quintet from Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) have served for between 25 and 45 years each, helping the trust port retain its crown as the premier gateway for Britain’s international trade.
Two of the five, Graham Lee and Jason Davis, work for HHA’s revered pilot launch service, with another, Mark Avenell, having recently moved to a managerial role supporting the authority’s trainees and apprentices.
Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) Duty Officer Sarah Chilver is also celebrating 40 years, while Marine Support Manager Adrian Britton has marked his 45th anniversary with the business.
Vanessa Mann, Head of People & Culture at HHA, said:
“We are delighted to celebrate the incredible achievements of Graham, Jason, Mark, Sarah and Adrian.
“We are hugely grateful for the commitment they have shown to us and our stakeholders, providing exceptional service from the very first day they joined us.
“So much will have changed over those years, yet that outstanding level of service has remained a constant throughout their time with us.
“When you consider the average length of time someone works for a UK employer stands between three and five years, making their achievements all the more amazing.”
HHA has won numerous awards for its commitment to its colleagues, including being crowned the Inclusive Workplace of the Year at the 2025 British Ports Association Awards and earning gold accreditation from Essex Working Well in 2024.
The business is also proud members of The 5% Club, a collection of organisations with at least 5% of its workforce in ‘earn and learn’ positions.
Vanessa added:
“We would not be the business we are today without the extraordinary contributions of colleagues like Graham, Jason, Mark, Sarah and Adrian.
“Their experience, knowledge and commitment have played a real part in shaping HHA over the years, and together they are a great example of the calibre of people we are fortunate to have working with us.”
Those looking to follow in the footsteps of the quintet can discover the latest career opportunities at HHA via www.hha.co.uk/about/careers .

https://hha.co.uk/feed/.title: Royal Navy joins forces with Freeport East and Harwich Haven Authority to showcase region’s maritime resilience
https://hha.co.uk/feed/.text:
HMS Severn docked at Harwich
Freeport East and Harwich Haven Authority (HHA) welcomed the Royal Navy to Harwich today [12 August 2026], bringing together senior figures from industry, local government and the maritime sector to showcase the future of regional resilience and security.
The event, Resilience in Harwich with the Royal Navy , took place on Wednesday 12 August at the Pier Hotel in Harwich and coincided with the docking of a Royal Navy River Class Offshore Patrol Vessel, HMS Severn, at Harwich – marking a rare visit that gave guests the opportunity to tour the ship.
Hosted jointly by Freeport East and HHA, and attended by a network of business, civic and industry leaders, the session brought the Royal Navy’s Naval Regional Command and Presentation team to Harwich to set out their vision for a ‘Hybrid Navy’, which would blend crewed platforms, autonomous systems and data and digital technology to deliver operational effect around the UK coastline.
Attendees heard directly from the Royal Navy about its plans for the region – including the county’s affiliation with the new Type 31 frigate HMS Venturer, formalised in 2024 and the first such link between Essex and a warship in 30 years. Currently under construction in Scotland and due to enter service later this decade, HMS Venturer connects more than 1.8 million people across Essex, from Colchester to Southend, with the Royal Navy’s next generation of frigates.
Freeport East’s Steve Beel addressed the strategic importance of Harwich to the UK’s maritime and defence footprint.
Steve Beel, CEO at Freeport East, said:
“It has been our pleasure to host the Royal Navy here in Harwich today and to have the opportunity to bring local industry and political leaders together to hear about the future of maritime resilience in the region. Harwich has always punched above its weight when it comes to maritime activity, from the days of Christopher Jones, the Harwich-born captain and part-owner of the Mayflower, through to the Kindertransport in the Second World War and on to being a prime link for millions of passengers to the European continent.  Days like this are a reminder that this coastline still matters both strategically and economically to the whole United Kingdom.”
Dr Jo North, CEO at Harwich Haven Authority, added:
“Harwich has always been a place where maritime expertise, innovation and collaboration come together, so it is a privilege to welcome the Royal Navy and so many partners to the Haven. As the organisation responsible for the safe navigation of one of the UK’s busiest and most strategically important waterways, Harwich Haven Authority know that strong partnerships and shared knowledge are at the heart of building a resilient and thriving maritime future.
“Bringing together industry, government and defence gives us the opportunity to share ideas, explore new technologies and strengthen the relationships that will support our region for years to come. By working together, we can unlock new opportunities for innovation, economic growth and skills, while ensuring our ports and coastal communities continue to play a vital role in the UK’s prosperity.”
Naval Regional Commander of London and Eastern England, Commodore Timothy Green CBE ADC said:
“I am delighted to join HMS SEVERN in Harwich this week.  This warship visit is an ideal opportunity to engage with the Maritime and Security communities in Essex and meet many Civic and Defence Industry leaders.
“Essex has a long and proud history of supporting the Royal Navy and this region remains a key maritime county with one of the largest coastlines in the UK.  Furthermore, Harwich remains a strategically vital port for both the region and the whole of the UK.
“I know that HMS SEVERN’s visit will further strengthen the very strong bonds between the Royal Navy and Essex.”
