https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Chairman’s Update: Building for the Next Chapter
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
Chairman’s Update: Building for the Next Chapter
Chelmsford City FC – A New Structure for an Exciting Future
Since taking over Chelmsford City Football Club, our ambition has always been clear: to build a successful and ambitious football club that our supporters, our community and our city can be proud of.
We’ve made significant progress over the past few years, both on and off the pitch. Attendances have grown, we’ve strengthened the club commercially, invested in our infrastructure and taken the important step towards becoming a full-time football club. But as I’ve said many times before,  better never stops.
If we’re serious about achieving our ambitions, which we are, we must continue to evolve, improve and put the right people and structures in place to take us to the next level. With that in mind, I’m pleased to announce a number of changes to the leadership and management structure of Chelmsford City FC.
A Stronger Advisory Board
We are restructuring our Advisory Board to create a more focused and accountable leadership team, bringing together individuals with the experience, expertise and passion to help drive the club forward.
Our new structure will be:
Chairman:  Spencer Gore
Vice Chairman:  Mat Starling
President:  David Selby
Fan Engagement Advisor:  Caroline Barker
Foundation Advisor:  Peter Feasey
Performance Advisor:  Jamil Qureshi
New additions :
Commercial Advisor:  Dan Healy – Chief Commercial Officer and owner at Gorely Group
Operations Advisor:   Andy Sleet – Founder, Freedom BC Ltd
Financial Advisor:  Dom Groves – Purchasing Director, BEW Electrical Distributors Ltd
Legal & Compliance Advisor:  Adam Jones – Partner, Birketts LLP
Managing Director:  Damian Irvine
Dan Watkins will continue to support the club as both shareholder and Director in an unchanged role. Rather than simply being an advisory body, members will take greater ownership of their respective areas, supporting the management team and helping shape the club’s future.
I’m particularly pleased that David Selby will become our new Club President. David has been a tremendous servant to Chelmsford City over many years, and his passion and commitment to the club make him an ideal person for this role. I’m also delighted that Mat Starling will become Vice Chairman, taking on a more prominent role as we continue to develop the club. We will be making further announcements about the new additions to the Advisory Board in the coming weeks so you can learn more about them.
I’d also like to take this opportunity to thank our outgoing President Paul Hopkins for his dedication and contribution to Chelmsford City over the years. His service to the club deserves recognition, and we will be paying a separate tribute.
A Major Step Forward: Our First Full-Time Managing Director
One of the most significant developments is the appointment of Damian Irvine as our first full-time Managing Director. This is an important milestone for Chelmsford City FC. As the club has grown, so too have the demands of running it. If we want to continue progressing through the football pyramid, we need experienced, dedicated leadership overseeing the day-to-day operation of the entire club.
In Damian, we have someone who understands football, has experience of leading clubs at our level and above, and shares our ambition for what Chelmsford City can become. Damian will have overall responsibility for the day-to-day running of the club, supported by a clearer and more streamlined management structure and will report directly to me. Again, we will post separately about this appointment in the coming days and weeks.
Harry Maynard will continue to oversee football operations, working closely with our management and coaching teams to continue developing the footballing side of the club. Keith Moule will oversee non-football operations, ensuring that everything behind the scenes continues to develop and improve.
Both will report directly to Damian, creating clear lines of responsibility

https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Match Report: Chelmsford City 1-0 Maidstone United
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
Chelmsford City returned to winning ways on Monday night, with a second-half Jack Barham penalty giving the Clarets a 1-0 win over Maidstone United.
City arrived off the back of a 2-2 draw at Walton & Hersham on Saturday. Barham scored twice in the first half, on 27 and 42 minutes, to put the Clarets two goals up at the break, but the hosts hit back through Makise Evans on 80 minutes and Kleyton Dowglas De Biazze Junior three minutes later to level it. Mark Cooper made two changes to the starting line-up, with Leo Sery and Cav Miley returning.
Tompkins was booked early on for pulling down Riley Court, giving Maidstone a free kick just outside the box. Court took it and aimed for the bottom right, but it swayed just past the net. A few minutes later Maidstone had another free kick, 30 yards out, which Court took once more. It was passed to Ryan Hanson, but Worman blocked. The Stones stayed on the attack as Marriott blocked a shot that just hit the top of the bar, giving United another opportunity, and Leech’s header went just wide to the left. Court had another shot on goal after United controlled the ball well around the box, but Marriott dived down to his left just in time.
City won the ball from Maidstone several times, and their first chance came when Clarke switched the ball over to the left for Green, who took a shot with too much power and sent it over the bar. Manny Egbo sent the ball down the right for Clarke, who passed it into the box, but United’s defence blocked Barham and Green from getting a touch. Maidstone found their footing again after a City spell, with Marriott brilliantly blocking a strike from Dermi Lusala.
On 31 minutes Sery came close to putting us ahead from Barbrook’s cross, but Holden did just enough to keep his close-range effort out. Clarke produced our best moment of the half on 37, driving at the heart of the defence and getting a shot away. His effort took a double deflection, leaving Holden beaten, but it went just wide. Miley was booked on 43.
In the fourth minute of first-half stoppage time Sery got on the end of the ball but was dragged down by a United player, and somehow it wasn’t given. Both sides were probably thankful to finish the half without conceding.
City made a much better start to the second half, with plenty of work between Barham and Green down the left. Sery almost got the opener with a spectacular header that went just over the bar.
Egbo was then fouled in the box, and City were awarded a penalty. Barham took it and scored on 55 minutes against his former club, his third goal in two days. Leo Hamblin was shown the yellow card for a foul on Egbo, giving City a free kick.
Tom Leahy found a dangerous opening down the right, but his ball into the box was blocked by Ralph. City regained possession after the substitutions of Odegah and Olopade, who made an instant impact. Clarke found an opportunity to shoot down the left, but it went wide.
There was some great play after Ronan came on. Barham delivered a strong ball from the right, and Ronan was first to take a shot, which rebounded to Green, who tried his luck from 25 yards, but a deflection sent it over the bar.
Cam Green was booked just before the 90-minute mark, giving Maidstone a dangerous free kick on the left, but Barbrook headed it away. Odegah was fouled down the left in the first minute of stoppage time, giving City another free kick. It didn’t lead to a second goal, and Green tried his luck from outside the box once more, but it swayed to the left.
Lusala tried one more shot at the very end, but it went wide to the left.
City will be pleased with that penalty, as it takes them seventh and into the play-off zone.
Full-time: Chelmsford City 1-0 Maidstone United
Chelmsford City:  Marriott, Barbrook, Tompkins, Ralph, Sery (Odegah 70′), Barham, Green, Miley (C), Egbo, Worman (Olopade 73′), Clarke (Ronan 82′).
Unused Substitutes: Eastwood, McFarlane, Dunne.
Goals:  Barham (55′)
Yellow Cards:  Tompkins (3′), Miley (43′), Clark

https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Match Report: Walton & Hersham 2-2 Chelmsford City
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
Chelmsford City were held to a 2-2 draw away at Walton & Hersham, despite a first-half brace from Jack Barham putting the Clarets two goals ahead at the break. Two goals in quick succession from the hosts in the second half saw Mark Cooper’s side leave Surrey with a point.
City travelled to Walton & Hersham looking to return to winning ways in the National League South following their FA Trophy exit against AFC Telford United the previous weekend. Ben Worman made his first league start since returning to the club on loan from Solihull Moors, while Jack Barham led the line for the Clarets.
The opening stages were relatively quiet, with neither side creating much in front of goal. City won the first corner of the afternoon on 10 minutes, opting to play it short to Worman, but his cross was blocked and possession returned to the hosts. Clarke began to cause problems down the left, delivering a dangerous ball into the box which Worman flicked on towards Harry Barbrook at the back post. However, the Walton & Hersham defence managed to cut it out for another corner.
This time, City opted to go long. Barham headed the ball back across goal towards Kian Ronan, whose header went straight up into the air before being headed back into the goalkeeper’s arms. The hosts had a good opportunity on 21 minutes following a quick counter-attack. Archy Taylor found himself in a promising position at the back post but mistimed his effort, with the ball trickling off him and out for a goal kick.
City took the lead on 27 minutes following a wonderfully worked team goal. Ash Clarke produced a moment of magic to keep possession under pressure before switching the play to Cam Green. Green headed the ball across into the path of Barham, who showed great composure to slot his effort underneath the oncoming Dillon Addai and into the net. It was Barham’s sixth league goal of the season and gave City the advantage.
The Clarets nearly doubled their lead just two minutes later. A free kick won by Clarke on the right was delivered into the box, where Ben Tompkins headed the ball back across goal. Barham was waiting to meet it with a close-range volley, but his effort went straight at Addai. City were beginning to take control of proceedings, with Clarke particularly influential in the attacking areas.
On 37 minutes, Clarke won another corner down the left. The Clarets again opted to take it short, finding Worman, who delivered a dangerous ball into the box. Tompkins saw his initial effort blocked before the ball fell to Ronan, whose powerful strike flew narrowly wide of the left-hand post.
Clarke became the first player to enter the referee’s book on 40 minutes, but just two minutes later, he was at the heart of another brilliant City move. The winger played a superb outside-of-the-boot pass into the path of Barham, who once again demonstrated his composure in front of goal, finishing into the bottom-right corner to double City’s advantage. It was Barham’s second goal of the afternoon and his seventh league goal of the campaign, sending the Clarets into the break with a two-goal lead.
Half-time: Walton & Hersham 0-2 Chelmsford City
The hosts made a change at the break, with Junior Dixon replacing Josh Ayres, before getting the second half underway. City looked to build on their impressive first-half performance, with Kian Ronan producing a lovely piece of skill early in the half, tracking back to regain possession before executing a roulette in midfield to escape pressure.
On 50 minutes, a loose pass from Denzelle Olopade presented Dixon with an opportunity for the hosts. With Alfie Marriott off his line, Dixon attempted an effort from distance but failed to hit the target. City responded two minutes later when Olopade threaded a pass through to Green. Rather than taking the shot himself, Green looked to square the ball across goal for Barham to complete his hat-trick, but the hosts managed to block the delivery.

https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Match Report: Telford United 1-1 Chelmsford City (Telford win 6-5 on penalties)
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
Chelmsford City’s FA Trophy run ended on penalties at AFC Telford United, after a 1-1 draw in which Green’s long-range strike was cancelled out by Cawthorne before half-time, and neither side could find a winner in an end-to-end second half.
Mark Cooper’s side travelled to Shropshire to begin their FA Trophy campaign. City arrived eighth in the National League South, with just one league defeat in their opening 16, and off a 2-1 home win over Farnborough and a 2-2 draw with Ebbsfleet United. Telford, 11th in the National League North, were unbeaten in their last five league games. There was no replay or extra time, so a draw meant penalties.
City made no changes to the starting line-up, but it was also the day that Ben Worman returned to the club on a short-term loan from National League side Solihull Moors.
City started brightly. Barham got the ball into the box from the right, almost giving Odegah a header on goal. On 5 minutes Clarke passed to Green, who sent the ball into the box from the left, but nobody was there. City won a free kick soon after, taken by Green, but it fell comfortably into the keeper’s hands. Barham made another great run down the right on 10, but again nobody was there to meet him. Telford had their first moment on 12, with good work on the left, but their ball into the box found nobody, and Ralph luckily chested it back to Marriott.
City took the lead on 20 minutes. A Barham free kick was cleared by Telford’s defence, but Green took a shot from 40 yards out and scored an absolute screamer, hitting the post before dropping into the net. 1-0 to City.
Telford then started to keep the ball around our box, until a foul on Miley by Moult on 29 relieved the pressure. Marriott made a fantastic diving save on 32 as Walker had a shot on goal from the left. City’s defence kept Telford out of the box, and Clarke made a great tackle and had a shot from the halfway line, but it had too much power and swayed to the left.
Telford equalised on 35 minutes. Ralph headed a corner away, but the ball fell back to Telford and Cawthorne found the back of the net to make it 1-1. On 40 minutes Cranston pulled down Barham on the left, giving City a free kick, taken by Green, but the Telford defence headed it away. On 45 Odegah did brilliantly to get away from Cawthorne down the left and, bearing down on goal with Barham open in the box, opted to shoot, but his effort was blocked.
At half-time Crowther replaced Green, who sustained an injury from an earlier tackle in the first half.
On 48 minutes City gave away a free kick when Olopade took down a Telford player, but fortunately it went just wide on the right. Odegah was booked on 50 and gave away another free kick, with the ball falling into the City box and being cleared by Crowther. Telford looked dangerous on 52 as a ball was launched in from the left, but Ralph headed it away for a corner. It landed in the path of Clarke, who drove the ball all the way to Telford’s box and had a shot that went just wide.
Olopade gave away another free kick on 55, which was launched into the box. A Telford player got a head on it, but Marriott saved brilliantly. Olopade was booked, and on 57 minutes Worman replaced him.
Benning was booked after taking down Odegah twice in twenty seconds, which gave City a free kick. Clarke took it and, after a battle in the box, the ball fell to Tompkins, who put it in the net, but the referee called it back for a foul on a Telford player.
On 61 minutes Marriott launched the ball out for Barham and Odegah, who linked up well, and Barham had a chance on goal, but it was blocked by Hall. https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.title: Welcome to City Ben Worman!
https://chelmsfordcityfc.com/feed/.text:
We are delighted to announce the signing of Midfielder Ben Worman from National League side Solihull Moors on a short-term loan deal.
The 25-year-old arrives at the Dunmow Group Community Stadium with plenty of experience having previously represented Cambridge United, Gateshead, Cork City and Weymouth.
The midfielder helps to give us legs in the middle of the park while also providing creativity to the side!
Worman began his career at Cambridge United and is still the youngster ever player to put on a U’s shirt, at 16 years old in 2017. Two years later his first loan spell actually came at Chelmsford City. Unfortunately he did not feature in a league game.
Following his departure from Cambridge United in 2023, Worman joined League of Ireland Premier Division side Cork City before returning to England in January 2024 to sign for National League side Gateshead.
The midfielder enjoyed a successful spell with the Heed, making 78 appearances across all competitions and helping the club lift the Isuzu FA Trophy at Wembley in 2024. Worman started the final against Solihull Moors and went on to make 52 appearances during the 2024/25 campaign.
His performances earned him a move to Solihull Moors in the summer of 2025, where he continued to gain valuable National League experience throughout the 2025/26 season.
Worman now returns to Chelmsford City, having previously joined the Clarets on loan from Cambridge United in November 2019, looking to bring his experience and quality to Mark Cooper’s midfield as City continue their Enterprise National League South campaign.
Welcome back to Chelmsford City, Ben!

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: JAY LOVETT JOINS BRETT MUNYARD’S MANAGEMENT TEAM
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town Football Club are delighted to announce the addition of Jay Lovett to Brett Munyard’s management team, with Jay taking up the role of First-Team Coach.
Jay arrives at The Arena with a wealth of experience across non-league football, having enjoyed a lengthy playing career before progressing into coaching and management.
As a player, Jay represented a number of clubs across the non-league pyramid, including Crawley Town, Brentford, Eastbourne Borough, Lewes and Whitehawk.
His playing career also saw him experience promotion success, helping Eastbourne Borough secure promotion to the Conference National via the Conference South play-offs in the 2007/08 season.
Following his transition into coaching, Jay spent four years working as a Youth Development Phase Coach at Brighton & Hove Albion, gaining valuable experience in player development before moving into senior management.
He has since held a number of positions across the non-league game, including spells with South Park, Burgess Hill Town and Haywards Heath Town, alongside coaching opportunities at Eastbourne Borough.
One of the highlights of his managerial career came during his second spell at Burgess Hill Town, where he returned in May 2024 as joint-manager alongside Gary Mansell.
The pair enjoyed a successful 2024/25 campaign, guiding Burgess Hill Town to promotion and further underlining Jay’s experience of building competitive sides and achieving success at this level.
More recently, Jay took charge of Whitehawk in the Isthmian Premier Division, before stepping down from the managerial role in October.
He now joins Brett and the rest of the coaching staff as the Blues continue to strengthen their first-team setup.
Everyone at Brentwood Town would like to warmly welcome Jay to the Club and wish him every success in his new role at The Arena.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town booked their place in the Fourth Round of the Velocity Cup on Tuesday evening, overcoming a spirited Bowers & Pitsea side 4-2 at The Arena in an entertaining six-goal encounter.
The Blues made a blistering start, with Bradley Sach finding the net twice inside the opening ten minutes to put Brett Munyard’s side firmly in control. However, the young visitors showed plenty of character to work their way back into the contest, with Ramsey McLachlan reducing the deficit before Ollie Peters restored Brentwood’s two-goal advantage with a well-taken free-kick.
Despite enjoying the majority of possession, Brentwood were unable to completely shake off their opponents, with Bowers continuing to threaten and forcing Jack Giddens into several important saves. The visitors also struck the crossbar shortly before half-time, ensuring there was still plenty to play for after the break.
The Blues emerged with renewed intent in the second half, creating several opportunities before substitute Freddie Sears eventually made it 4-1 in the 76th minute, reacting quickest to a loose ball following a goalmouth scramble.
There was still time for one final talking point, however, as Bowers were awarded a late penalty following contact between substitute Danny Hanson and Brentwood captain Matt Cripps. The decision prompted protests from the home skipper, but Hanson kept his composure from the spot to make it 4-2.
While the late goal gave the scoreline a slightly different complexion, Brentwood comfortably saw out the closing stages to secure their progression into the next round.
There was also plenty of encouragement to take from the evening beyond the result, with two U23s players, Fenton Tucker and Ruben Kibrom, named in the starting XI. Tucker, in particular, impressed at right-back, producing a confident performance and testing Bowers goalkeeper Lenny Perry with a well-struck second-half effort. Callum Goodey and Sam Bryan also featured from the bench, providing further first-team opportunities for the club’s younger players.
Bowers deserve credit for their performance, too. Having already progressed through two previous rounds with their young Reserves side, they continued that approach at The Arena and showed plenty of quality, energy and determination throughout the evening.

Brett Munyard made several changes to his starting XI, with Max Hudson, Luke Read and Louie Kudiabor all coming into the side after featuring from the bench in Saturday’s victory at Wingate & Finchley.
Benas Vaivada also returned to the starting line-up following a short spell with Walthamstow to gain valuable fitness and game time, while U23s duo Tucker and Kibrom were handed their opportunities.
The Blues made a bright start and were rewarded for their patient approach in the seventh minute. A well-worked move saw Max Hudson pick out Vaivada advancing down the left flank, with the returning winger’s cross flicked into the path of Sach by Hudson. The striker made no mistake, firing first time beyond Lenny Perry to open the scoring.
Just three minutes later, Sach doubled his tally and Brentwood’s advantage. This time, Ollie Peters provided the assist with a beautifully weighted through ball, sending Sach through one-on-one with Perry. The forward kept his composure to slot home and put The Blues firmly in control.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: THREE PLAYERS DEPART BRENTWOOD TOWN
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town can confirm that Aiden Prall, Suley Zuhdu and Wyan Reid have departed the club.
AIDEN PRALL
Aiden initially joined The Blues on a 28-day loan from Ramsgate in January 2026, with his stay extended the following month after impressing between the sticks.
His performances throughout the second half of the campaign played an important part in Brentwood’s push towards the Isthmian League Premier Division play-off final, with his shot-stopping ability, distribution and consistency proving valuable as the season progressed.
Aiden remained at The Arena ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, although injuries have unfortunately restricted his opportunities this season.
In total, the goalkeeper made 30 appearances in Brentwood colours, keeping seven clean sheets during his time with the club.
SULEY ZUHDU
Suley arrived at Brentwood in September 2026 from Buckhurst Hill, having previously worked under manager Brett Munyard during his time at Aveley.
The forward added another attacking option to The Blues’ squad and made an impact during his time at The Arena, scoring twice in eight appearances across all competitions.
With the club’s cup commitments limiting his opportunities, Suley was unable to feature as regularly as he would have liked, but we thank him for his efforts and contribution during his time in Sky Blue.
WYAN REID
A familiar and much-loved face amongst Brentwood supporters, Wyan Reid has enjoyed several spells with the club and leaves having made a lasting impression on those who have followed The Blues home and away.
Wyan first joined ahead of the 2020/21 campaign, which was unfortunately curtailed due to the COVID-19 pandemic, before returning midway through the 2023/24 season as Brentwood reached the Isthmian League North play-off final.
Following a departure at the end of that campaign, Wyan briefly returned during the 2024/25 season, making an appearance away at Waltham Abbey, before joining Walthamstow.
He would return once again ahead of the 2025/26 season, playing an important role as The Blues embarked on their return to the Isthmian Premier Division. A regular presence at right-back, Wyan featured prominently throughout the campaign, also getting himself on the scoresheet away at Chichester City as Brentwood secured another play-off final appearance, this time against Billericay Town.
His latest spell brings his overall Brentwood appearance tally to 97, just three short of the coveted century, with six goals scored across his various spells in Sky Blue.
THANK YOU, AIDEN, SULEY AND WYAN!
Everyone at Brentwood Town would like to thank Aiden, Suley and Wyan for their commitment, professionalism and contributions to the club.
We wish all three nothing but the very best for the next chapters of their careers, and they will always be welcome back at the Brentwood Arena.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Brentwood Complete Comeback Victory in North London
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town made it back-to-back league victories with an impressive second-half comeback, overturning a first-half deficit to secure a valuable 2-1 win away at Wingate & Finchley.
After a relatively even opening period, the hosts took the lead just after the half-hour mark through Caoilan McGettigan, although there was frustration in the Brentwood ranks as the goal came following a challenge on Matt Cripps which went unpunished by the referee.
The Blues responded positively and, despite going into the break behind, emerged with renewed attacking intent. Their pressure was eventually rewarded when George Saunders’ excellent delivery was turned home by Charlie Edwards, before Ollie Peters calmly converted a late penalty to complete the turnaround and register his first goal in a Brentwood shirt.
There was further drama surrounding both sides of the pitch, with a member of the Wingate & Finchley bench dismissed following the equaliser and the hosts left frustrated by the decision to award Brentwood’s winning penalty. Jack Giddens also played his part at the other end, producing two important saves, including a superb stop deep into stoppage time to preserve all three points.
It was another encouraging afternoon for Brett Munyard’s side, who made it two wins from two on the road and continued their recent upward momentum.
MATCH REPORT
There was little to separate the sides during the opening exchanges, with Wingate & Finchley initially looking the more comfortable of the two teams.
However, Brentwood gradually grew into the contest and began to threaten through the deliveries of George Saunders. His low, dangerous cross into the area forced Charlie Grainger into a block to prevent the ball reaching a Brentwood shirt, before another inviting delivery from a free-kick down the right-hand side narrowly evaded everyone in the penalty area.
The Blues continued to apply pressure and, on 24 minutes, a short corner from Saunders found Alfie Cerulli on the edge of the box. The forward made room for a shot, but his low effort was comfortably gathered by Grainger.
Despite Brentwood’s growing influence, it was the hosts who broke the deadlock on 32 minutes.
There was a sense of frustration from the visitors as Matt Cripps appeared to be pushed by Anointed Chukwu in the build-up, but play was allowed to continue. Wingate quickly broke forward through captain Ryan Lowe, who released Caoilan McGettigan in behind the Brentwood defence. The winger found himself one-on-one with Giddens before calmly placing his effort beyond the goalkeeper to make it 1-0.
The Blues responded almost immediately and came agonisingly close to restoring parity. Cerulli caused problems inside the Wingate penalty area before the ball eventually fell to Saunders, whose close-range effort was kept out by a superb goal-line save from Grainger. Andy Freeman then saw his follow-up effort deflected behind for a corner.
Brentwood continued to push for an equaliser before the interval, with another dangerous Saunders delivery finding Jayden Gipson inside the area. The defender connected with a header, but his effort flashed narrowly wide of the far post as the hosts held onto their advantage.
The Blues emerged from the interval with renewed purpose and immediately set about searching for an equaliser.
Their persistence paid off on 54 minutes. Cerulli won a free-kick down the left-hand side, allowing Saunders another opportunity to deliver into the danger area. His excellent cross was met by the head of Charlie Edwards, who produced a clever flick to guide the ball beyond Grainger and into the net.
It was a deserved leveller for Brentwood, whose attacking deliveries had caused problems throughout the afternoon.

https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: BRENTWOOD TOWN FC EXTENDS LONG-STANDING PARTNERSHIP WITH SHEPHERD NEAME IN NEW THREE-YEAR DEAL
https://www.brentwoodtownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Brentwood Town Football Club is delighted to announce the extension of its long-standing partnership with Shepherd Neame, with both parties agreeing to a new three-year sponsorship deal.
The agreement represents another significant chapter in a relationship that has continued to benefit both organisations, strengthening the connection between the club and one of the UK’s most established brewing and pub businesses.
Shepherd Neame has been a valued partner of Brentwood Town FC for a number of years, playing an important role in supporting the club and its ongoing development, both on and off the pitch.
The new agreement will see the partnership continue for a further three years, building on the foundations already established and creating further opportunities for both organisations to work together.
Founded in 1698, Shepherd Neame is Britain’s oldest brewer, with a rich heritage spanning more than 325 years. Based in Faversham, Kent, the independent family business is renowned for producing a wide range of award-winning beers, alongside operating 280 pubs across London and the South East.
With a shared appreciation for tradition, community and bringing people together, the continued relationship reflects the importance of strong partnerships and the positive impact they can have.
Brentwood Town FC Chairman, Jez Dickinson, said:
“Shepherd Neame have been fantastic supporters of our football club for a number of years, and we’re delighted to extend this partnership for a further three years. We really value their continued support and look forward to building on our relationship together.”
Dougie Dick, Business Development Manager at Shepherd Neame, added:
“We are delighted to continue our partnership with Brentwood Town and look forward to more success on and off the field.”
Brentwood Town FC would like to place on record its sincere thanks to Dougie and everyone at Shepherd Neame for their continued support and commitment to the club.
We look forward to working together over the next three years and continuing what has already been a hugely positive partnership.
Our Club. Your Town. Brentwood Town.

https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.text:
Joe White is a Dagger
Dagenham & Redbridge are delighted to announce the signing of midfielder Joe White on a deal until the end of the season.
White returns to Victoria Road, having previously come through the Daggers' academy before making his first-team debut in November 2016.
The Camden-born midfielder made six senior appearances for the club during his first spell, scoring once, before departing for Stevenage in January 2018.
After leaving Stevenage, White continued his development with spells at Wealdstone and Biggleswade Town, where he enjoyed an impressive goalscoring record, finding the net 23 times in 34 appearances during his first spell.
He subsequently joined Hendon in January 2020, where he established himself as an influential figure, scoring 67 goals in 168 appearances across all competitions. He also captained the side during the 2022/23 season.
White moved to Hemel Hempstead Town in December 2024, reuniting with Daggers manager Lee Allinson, under whom he had previously worked at both Biggleswade Town and Hendon.
Primarily operating as an attacking midfielder, White brings creativity and a goalscoring threat to the Daggers' midfield, having registered double figures in front of goal during multiple seasons at Step 3 and Step 2 level.
Now, he returns to the club where his senior career began, ready to make his mark once again in a Daggers shirt.
Welcome back to Victoria Road, Joe!

https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.title: 26/27 Match Report: Tonbridge Angels (H)
https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.text:
Dagenham & Redbridge produced an impressive second-half performance to secure a convincing 4-1 victory over Tonbridge Angels at Victoria Road.
The Daggers started brightly and created an early opportunity when Kayden Harrack lofted a cross towards the back post, only for a Tonbridge defender to intervene and clear the danger.
Harry Beautyman was next to threaten after a cleverly taken free-kick sent him through on goal, but his effort towards the near post was well saved by the visiting goalkeeper.
At the other end, Ashmore was called into action, brilliantly tipping a low effort from the visitors away to keep the scores level.
Rodari then came close to opening the scoring. Vincent delivered a superb cross into the box, finding Campbell at the back post. The striker nodded the ball back across goal towards his strike partner, but Rodari could only direct his header over the crossbar.
The breakthrough soon followed, however, and it was Beautyman who provided the finish. Campbell’s flick-on found the Daggers skipper, who struck a superb half-volley into the bottom corner to give the hosts the lead.
Tonbridge responded and found an equaliser through Thompson, who finished from close range to ensure the sides went into the interval level.
Half-Time: Daggers 1-1 Tonbridge Angels
The Daggers came out after the break looking to regain their advantage and nearly did so when Addae did brilliantly down the right-hand side before delivering for Campbell, whose header crashed against the crossbar.
Sam Graham also went close, seeing his effort kept out by a superb save from Harness in the Tonbridge goal. The goalkeeper required treatment following the intervention, but was able to continue.
The hosts continued to press and were rewarded in the 75th minute. Harrack picked up possession and unleashed a powerful left-footed effort to restore the Daggers’ lead.
Just four minutes later, the advantage was doubled. Clayden delivered a delicious cross into the penalty area, where Campbell rose to meet it and powered his header into the net to make it 3-1.
The scoring was completed shortly afterwards when a mistake from the Tonbridge goalkeeper presented an opportunity for Antony Papadopoulos, who capitalised to put the result beyond doubt.
It was a dominant second-half display from the Daggers, who found the net three times after the break to secure all three points at Victoria Road.
Full-Time: Daggers 4-1 Tonbridge Angels
Daggers Starting XI: Ashmore, Adenola, Graham, Hawkins, Addae (Moulton 89′), Vincent, Marsh, Harrack, Beautyman (Papadopoulos 72′), Campbell, Rodari (Clayden 55′).
Unused Substitutes: Ogayi, Bateson, Makowski.
Attendance: 1,248 (58 away)

https://daggers.co.uk/feed/.text:
Dagenham & Redbridge secured a hard-fought 1-0 victory away at AFC Totton, with Rodari’s early goal proving enough to claim all three points on the road.
The Daggers made the perfect start and took the lead after just eight minutes. A dangerous delivery from Addae caused problems for the Totton goalkeeper, who could only spill the cross into the path of Rodari. The striker reacted quickest to the loose ball, making no mistake from close range to put the visitors ahead.
Totton looked to respond and came close to an equaliser in the 21st minute when Sims struck the woodwork, giving the Daggers an early warning of the hosts’ threat.
Five minutes later, Rodari nearly doubled his tally after a mistake from Gosney presented the forward with an opportunity. However, the goalkeeper recovered in time to gather the ball and prevent a second Daggers goal.
The hosts continued to threaten as the half progressed, with a significant opportunity arriving shortly before the break. Godziemski saw his initial effort saved by Ashmore, before the rebound fell to Vigrass, who fired over the crossbar from a promising position.
Despite the pressure, the Daggers remained organised and took their one-goal advantage into the interval.
Half-Time: AFC Totton 0-1 Daggers
The second half saw Totton continue their search for an equaliser, with the Daggers having to work hard defensively to protect their lead.
Ashmore was called into action in the 62nd minute, producing a solid save to keep the hosts at bay as Totton looked to make their pressure count.
The game became increasingly competitive as the minutes ticked away, with Godziemski receiving a yellow card in the 89th minute following an incident involving Graham, who caught the defender on the head with his studs.
Totton pushed forward in the closing stages and came agonisingly close to finding a late equaliser. A long throw caused problems inside the Daggers penalty area, with the ball bouncing around before falling to Mills. His effort was well saved by Ashmore, but the rebound dropped to Godziemski, who could only find the side netting.
The Daggers stood firm through the closing moments, showing determination and resilience to see out the contest and secure a valuable away victory.
Full-Time: AFC Totton 0-1 Daggers
Starting XI: Ashmore, Adenola, Graham (90+2′), Hawkins, Addae (Moulton 59′), Vincent, Marsh, Harrack, Beautyman (Makowski 83′), Carroll (Papadopoulos 77′), Rodari (Campbell 63′).

https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.title: IFL Partners with Essex Cricket
https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Cricket is delighted to announce a new partnership with IFL, who have agreed to a three-year partnership with the Club.
International Food Link (IFL) is a specialist food and beverage supply chain business, supporting some of the world’s leading restaurant groups, quick-service restaurant chains (QSR) and food brands with their international growth. From its operations in the UK and Spain, IFL provides end-to-end solutions spanning global freight, food-grade warehousing, fulfilment, compliance and distribution, helping customers move products efficiently and reliably across international markets.
As part of the new agreement, IFL will become the sponsor of the collar on both the Men's and Women's T20 playing shirts. In addition, IFL will sponsor the Essex Women's Player of the Match awards throughout the 2027 T20 Blast campaign.
The partnership will also provide IFL with brand exposure across Essex Cricket's digital platforms, including the Club's official website and social media channels.
On the agreement, Lorraine Fletcher, Head of Business Operations at Essex Cricket, said: "We are really happy to welcome IFL on board as a new partner and into the Essex Cricket family.
“It is fantastic to have their support across both our Men’s and Women’s teams, particularly their involvement in our T20 playing shirts and Essex Women’s Player of the Match awards.
“We look forward to working closely with IFL and developing a successful partnership both on and off the field.”
Director at IFL, Paul Cooper, added: “We are proud to be partnering with Essex Cricket, a club with such a strong heritage and a real commitment to growing the game across both its Men’s and Women’s teams.
“Sponsoring the collar of the T20 playing shirts and the Essex Women’s Player of the Match awards gives us a fantastic opportunity to be part of the Club’s story over the next three years.
“We look forward to working closely with everyone at Essex Cricket and building a partnership that delivers real value for the Club, its supporters and our business.”

https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.title: Essex Cricket and WBS Logistics Renew Partnership
https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Cricket is pleased to announce that its partnership with WBS Logistics has been extended for a further three years.
Founded in 2003, WBS Logistics is an established logistics and freight forwarding company specialising in domestic and international transportation, warehousing, fulfilment, groupage and customs consultancy services. With over 20 years of industry experience, WBS provides tailored, reliable logistics solutions to businesses across a wide range of sectors, with a strong focus on customer service and building long-term relationships.
Committed to continued growth, service excellence and improving its environmental performance, Essex Cricket and WBS Logistics are proud to extend their partnership for a further three years.
As part of their renewed agreement, WBS will retain its sponsorship rights on the back of both the Men's and Women's T20 shirts, with its branding positioned centrally above each player's name and number.
WBS will also retain the branding rights for the Graham Napier 152 Bar, located behind the Doug Insole Pavilion. The bar is a popular section of the ground where Members and supporters can congregate, socialise and enjoy refreshments on matchdays.
Additionally, the logistics company will retain a pitch-facing advertising board, located alongside the main scoreboard, as well as digital advertising opportunities across the Club's platforms.
On the agreement, Lorraine Fletcher, Head of Business Operations at Essex Cricket, said: "We are delighted to be extending our partnership with WBS Logistics for another three years. Since joining Essex Cricket, WBS has become a valued partner of the Club, and we are looking forward to continuing to build on the strong relationship we have developed.
“Their support across both our Men’s and Women’s teams, as well as the wider Club, is hugely appreciated. Partnerships like this play an important role in helping us both grow and we look forward to working together over the next three seasons and building on the success we have already achieved.”
WBS Logistics Managing Director, David Burnham, added: "We are delighted to be extending our partnership with Essex Cricket for a further three years. Having built a strong relationship over the past three years, we are proud to continue supporting the Club, it's Men's and Women's teams and the wider Essex Cricket Community.
"At WBS, we believe in building long-term relationships with organisations that share our values and ambitions. Essex Cricket's commitment to its community, continued development and growing focus on sustainability strongly aligns with our own values as a business.
"We are committed to continually improving our own environmental performance and believe that supporting organisations with similar ambitions is an important part of that journey.
"We look forward to continuing our partnership and being part of Essex Cricket's success over the next three years."

https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.title: Essex Cricket and Woodland Group Renew Long-Standing Partnership
https://essexcricket.org.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Cricket is thrilled to announce that Principal Partner Woodland Group will continue its partnership with the Club throughout the 2027, 2028 and 2029 seasons, set to mark more than fifteen years of support.
Following its headline sponsorship of Essex Cricket's 150th Anniversary celebrations in 2026, Woodland Group will retain a prominent presence across playing kits, player awards and ground advertising.
As part of the renewed agreement, Woodland Group will retain its position as front-of-shirt sponsor of the Men's County Championship playing shirt for the 2027 season, alongside sponsorship of the front and non-leading arm of the Men's and Women's T20 shirt.
The partnership will also see Woodland Group continue its involvement in recognising individual player performances, sponsoring the Men's Player of the Year award and the Men's T20 Player of the Match award. In 2027, Woodland Group will also take on the sponsorship of the Men's Player of the Month awards.
Woodland Group's presence will extend beyond the playing shirts and awards, with the naming rights to the Woodland Group Stand also being retained. The popular remote-control truck is also set to return to the Ambassador Cruise Line Ground for both Men's and Women's T20 fixtures. The truck will once again deliver the match ball to the umpires, providing an added attraction for supporters throughout the competition.
With Woodland Group's support for Essex County Cricket Club totalling 15 years, its continued commitment represents a significant milestone in a partnership built on shared values, ambition and a passion for supporting the Club both on and off the field.
Ravi Bopara, Sir Alastair Cook and Ryan ten Doeschate pictured in the 2016 Woodland sponsored playing shirt.
On the agreement, Lorraine Fletcher, Head of Business Operations at Essex Cricket, said: "We are absolutely delighted to be continuing our partnership with Woodland Group for another three seasons. They have been part of the Essex Cricket family for 15 years, and during that time we have built a fantastic relationship based on shared values, trust and a genuine commitment to supporting one another.
"The support Woodland Group provides means so much to the Club. From their presence on our playing kits to their support of our player awards and matchday experience, Woodland Group has been an integral part of the Club for many years. We are incredibly grateful for their continued support, and for the confidence they continue to place in us.
"We are looking forward to working closely with their incredible team over the coming years and creating many more great memories for our players, supporters, Members and Partners together."
Kevin Stevens, Chairman and CEO at Woodland Group, added: “We are incredibly proud to continue our partnership with Essex Cricket for a further three years. After more than 15 years together, the relationship has grown into something that means a great deal to everyone at Woodland Group.
“Essex Cricket is an important part of the community we share, and throughout our partnership we have seen a real alignment in our values, our ambitions and the way both organisations want to make a positive impact beyond the boundary.
“Following the Club’s 150th Anniversary celebrations, we are delighted to be continuing that journey into 2027, 2028 and 2029. We are excited about what the next chapter will bring, and we look forward to supporting the players, Members, supporters and everyone connected with Essex Cricket for many more seasons to come.”

Essex Men's 2027 T20 Blast campaign begins with a visit to Hove to face Sussex Sharks, whilst Essex Women will travel to The Oval to take on Surrey.
The Men's and Women's T20 Blast fixtures have been released, with the opening matches of both campaigns set to take place away from home. Essex Men will begin their campaign against Sussex Sharks on Friday 21 May, whilst the Women will face Surrey at the Kia Oval on Sunday 23 May.
The first T20 action of the summer at the Ambassador Cruise Line Ground will arrive on Friday 28 May , with a blockbuster opening home fixture as Essex Men host Kent Spitfires Men in part one of the Battle of the Bridge! Meanwhile, Essex Women will play their first home T20 Blast fixture when newly Tier One Glamorgan Women visit Chelmsford on Sunday 30 May, in a double-header alongside the Men's clash against Middlesex.
Outside of their usual South Group opponents, Essex Men will make the rare trip up the A1 to face Durham Men at Banks Homes Riverside on Sunday 06 June, before returning to Chelmsford to host Warwickshire Bears Men on Sunday 04 July. The Men's group stage will reach its penultimate fixture with a trip to the Utilita Bowl to face Hampshire Hawks Men on Friday 09 July, before concluding at Lord's against Middlesex Men on Sunday 11 July.
Essex Women will face Glamorgan Women in the T20 format for the first time in the Club's history when they welcome the Welsh side to Chelmsford for their opening home fixture on Sunday 30 May. Their non-knockout phase will reach its penultimate fixture when Surrey Women visit the Ambassador Cruise Line Ground on Friday 09 July, before Essex Women travel north to face Lancashire Women on Sunday 11 July.
The T20 Blast will take centre stage on the cricket calendar for the Finals Day weekend, when no men’s or women’s international cricket is scheduled. T20 Blast Men’s Finals Day will once again be hosted at EdgBLASTon on Saturday 17 July with the T20 Blast Women’s Finals Day to be staged at Trent Bridge the next day. https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Sport in Essex takes centre stage with new initiative to boost health and wellbeing
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Essex United by Sport will help residents lead more active lives and improve access to physical activity.
A major new initiative has launched in Essex to help residents lead healthier lives. Essex United by Sport will bring together partners from across the county. Together they will use the power of sport to improve health and tackle inequalities.
Essex is home to world-class sporting facilities, elite teams and inspirational athletes. Essex United by Sport will build on these strengths to celebrate sporting achievements. It will bring people of all ages together and create opportunities to take part.
Essex United by Sport is powered by Essex County Council. It is delivered in partnership with Active Essex and their partners. Active Essex is the lead for sport and physical activity in Essex.
The programme will focus on:
sport for all – ensuring every resident can engage in sport
sport for communities – using sport to bring people together and strengthen local neighbourhoods
sport for health – helping residents live longer, healthier and happier lives
sport for the future – helping residents fulfil their potential and contributing to Essex’s economy.
While progress has been made, more than half a million adults in Essex still do not get the recommended 150 minutes of physical activity each week. This shows more needs to be done to help people get active.
Councillor Chris Hossack, Essex County Council Cabinet Member for Residents and Communities said:
“Sport and physical activity have the power to improve lives, strengthen communities and create opportunities for people of all ages. Essex United by Sport will bring together partners from the sport, health, education, criminal justice and voluntary and community sector, to ensure more residents can access those benefits, regardless of their background, location or ability.
“From supporting healthier lifestyles and improving mental health, to developing skills and inspiring future generations, this programme will help unlock the full potential of sport across Essex.”
The programme was launched at the Essex Sport Arena, University of Essex, on Tuesday 3 November.
Pupils from Braiswick Primary School joined players and coaches for a basketball game. Guests heard from speakers representing the council, Sport England and the sporting community. Topics included the role Essex United by Sport will play in creating healthier, more connected communities.
Lewis Richardson, Olympic medallist and Essex athlete attended the launch, and said:
“Sport has given me opportunities, experiences and life skills that have shaped who I am today. Every young person should have the chance to experience those benefits, regardless of where they live or their background. Essex United by Sport is about creating those opportunities and inspiring the next generation to get active, build confidence and achieve their potential.”
For further information, visit activeessex.org/essex-united-by-sport
The post Sport in Essex takes centre stage with new initiative to boost health and wellbeing appeared first on Active Essex .

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Thurrock Celebrates Double Success at Department for Education HAF Awards
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
The Thurrock Holiday Activities and Food (HAF) programme has been recognised on the national stage, with local provider JTD Arts named Regional HAF Provider of the Year and Owen Jarvis, a young leader who attends Arts Outburst, receiving the National HAF Young Person of the Year Award, announced by Joe Wicks.
Delivered locally through Essex ActivAte and funded by the Department for Education and Thurrock Council, the programme provides free holiday activities, nutritious meals and enriching experiences for children and young people eligible for income-related free school meals.
Presented at the Queen Elizabeth II Centre in London, JTD Arts was crowned Regional HAF Provider of the Year in recognition of its commitment to creating inclusive, welcoming opportunities for children and families across Thurrock.
Since joining the HAF programme in 2022, JTD Arts has built a strong reputation for its SEND-inclusive approach, ensuring children of all abilities can participate together and feel part of the same experience. Alongside a varied programme of physical activity, creative sessions and trips, JTD Arts provides ongoing support for families throughout the year, helping to reduce isolation and build stronger community connections. V
Victoria Jarmyn, Founder and Director of JTD Arts reflected:
“This award means so much more than recognition. It reflects the children, young people and families at the heart of our work and celebrates our team’s passion for creating inclusive opportunities where every child feels valued, supported and able to be the best they can be We’re incredibly proud that our commitment to inclusion, community and breaking down barriers has been recognised in this way.”
Thurrock also celebrated individual success as Owen Jarvis was named National HAF Young Person of the Year, with the award announced by fitness campaigner Joe Wicks via a special video message.
Over the past three years, Owen has grown from a quiet participant into a confident young leader and HAF ambassador. Through his involvement with ATF and Arts Outburst, he now volunteers at holiday sessions, supports younger children and promotes active, healthy lifestyles. His journey has even led to paid employment at his local tennis club.
His dedication and leadership make him a role model for other young people and a fantastic example of the lasting impact of the HAF programme.
Daryl Branch, Artistic Director & CEO at Arts Outburst told us:
“We’re incredibly proud of Owen and delighted to see him recognised as National HAF Young Person of the Year. Through our Young Leaders programme, we aim to give young people the confidence and opportunities to reach their potential, and Owen is a fantastic example of that. Seeing his achievements recognised nationally means so much. Congratulations, Owen!
Owen’s dad, Neil Jarvis also reflected:
“It was inspiring to hear the impact the programme is having across the country, and I’m incredibly proud of Owen for the hard work he’s put in. The opportunity has helped build his confidence and strengthened his ambitions for a future career in coaching.”
Owen also told us:
“I was proud to receive both the Regional and National Young Person of the Year awards at the HAF Awards 2026. The recognition reflects my dedication to supporting children and staff throughout the summer with Arts Outburst’s HAF programme in Thurrock. I am grateful for the opportunities and experiences I have gained through the programme and would like to thank Arts Outburst and Active Essex for their support. Congratulations to all the other winners.”
These awards shine a spotlight on the incredible work taking place across Thurrock through the Essex ActivAte programme, demonstrating how high-quality holiday provision can help children and young people stay active, build confidence, develop new skills and create brighter futures.

Nominations are now open for the Essex Activity awards 2026, celebrating the individuals, clubs, organisations and community champions who are making a difference through sport, physical activity and wellbeing across Greater Essex.
This year’s awards, sponsored by HolidayActivities, are particularly special as Active Essex celebrates 20 years of recognising sporting excellence and community impact through the Essex sports awards.
Residents are being asked to nominate individuals, organisations, clubs, workplaces and schools that have gone above and beyond to inspire and support their communities in becoming more active or achieved something outstanding in the past year.
Categories include Sports Personality, previously won by sporting stars such as Max Whitlock, Bethany Shriever and Michelle Agyemang, and Young Sports Personality where Alex Dowsett, Ellie Challis and Max Dowman have previously taken home the title. The awards will also honour dedicated volunteers through the Essex Activity Hero category, reflecting on those incredible unsung heroes in communities. Previous recipients include Lee Clark and parkrun’s Gerry McGovern, whose contributions helped strengthen connections through sport and physical activity.
Meanwhile categories such as Sports Club of the Year, Strengthening Communities Award and Active Employer of the Year will hope to celebrate the organisations using the power of sport and physical activity to transform lives and strengthen local communities. Popular categories such as Move With Us Champion, Inspiring Young Lives and Active Education Provider, recognise those who have gone above and beyond to create opportunities for children, and inspire other young people to embrace an active lifestyle.
Dr William Bird MBE, Chair of Active Essex said:
“The fact we’re celebrating 20 years of sports awards in Essex this year, is a triumph in itself, but every year I continue to be amazed by the incredible individuals, coaches, organisations and clubs that demonstrate outstanding commitment to helping people get active and discover the sport and activities they enjoy. I would encourage everyone to take a moment to nominate those making a difference in their community, so we can celebrate and recognise their exceptional contributions together.”
Marking two decades of inspiring stories, remarkable achievements and dedicated individuals, the annual event will honour some of Essex’s most inspiring individuals and organisations at an awards ceremony later this year. Whether it’s a motivating coach, a dedicated volunteer, an inspiring young person, an innovative school or a welcoming community group that are bringing people together through sport, the Essex Activity Awards are an opportunity to ensure their efforts receive the recognition they deserve.
Nominations close at midnight on Wednesday 30 th September 2026 .
To view the full list of categories and submit your nomination, visit the webpage: www.activeessex.org/essex-activity-awards-2026

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Green Spaces and Parks Activated to bring Communities Together
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Find Your Active HERE signs launch in Harlow and Thurrock to help residents move more in their local spaces.
Residents in Harlow and Thurrock are being encouraged to get active closer to home, thanks to the launch of Find Your Active Here signs. The initiative, launched at the beginning of August, aims to help local people discover simple, free and accessible ways to be active for community connection and belonging.
In partnership with Harlow Town Council, Thurrock Council and local organisations such as Time for Change, the Find Your Active Here signs are being piloted in two of the Sport England Place Partnership areas, Harlow (The Stow and Harlow Town Park) and Thurrock (Daisy Field, Tilbury).
A community hub with wide open space, The Stow Sports Ground is perfect for playful movement, group activities, and family fun. In addition, Harlow Town Park is a huge 164‑acre green space with gardens, play areas, trails, table tennis tables, a paddling pool, a skate park, and of course the outdoor gym. Both locations are an ideal space to encourage activity for every age, ability and confidence level.
Daisy Field is a local green space at the heart of Tilbury, serving as a focal point for the neighbourhood, frequently hosting local youth sports, wellness hubs, and community outreach. Daisy Field makes up a whole host of local, nearby green spaces that also include an outdoor gym, pump track, skate park, playground and walking circuit.
Danielle Warnes, Active Essex Relationship Manager for West Essex said; “We believe that being active doesn’t have to mean joining a gym or signing up for a class. Sometimes, the best place to move more, feel better, and enjoy the outdoors is right on your doorstep. Harlow is bursting with regeneration and this builds on the momentum to enhance local assets and give back to the community.”
The bright and visible signs include a QR code which signposts users to solo activities, or ways to get active with family, friends or neighbours. A host of inclusive options and organised sessions taking place in the green space, or nearby areas, can also be discovered. Since the placement of the signs at the beginning of the month, over 200 residents have already been inspired.
Juliette Raison, Active Essex Relationship Manager for South West Essex added: “Greater Essex is made up of 21% of green infrastructure and so many spaces are underutilised. It is our hope that these signs bring communities to these areas and encourage both informal and formal activity to take place. Being active outdoors brings so many added benefits for our mental health, social connection and wider physical health too.”
The introduction of the signs are part of the wider Find Your Active, Move for your Mind campaign that spans Greater Essex and is powered by Mind in Essex. The campaign highlights the powerful connection between physical activity and mental wellbeing, and acts as a gentle reminder that being active can be simple, uplifting, and part of your everyday life.
Find out more: www.activeessex.org/find-your-active/here/

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex ActivAte returns for summer 2026
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Free food and activities for children and young people this summer.
Families across Essex and Thurrock can now book clubs for the summer holidays. The clubs give children opportunities to stay active, try new sport and enjoy healthy meals in a safe and supportive environment. Free places are primarily available for children who get income-related Free School Meals (FSM).
They will get a Holiday Activities voucher code sent directly through their school. This means they can get priority access for bookings. Activities include a mix of sport and physical activity, creative and enrichment sessions, and fun food education. This helps children build confidence, make friends and develop new skills.
Bookings for the summer programme are now open. View more here!
Councillor Chris Hossack, Essex County Council Cabinet Member for residents and community services said:
“Our free holiday clubs are more important than ever. Not only do they make sure children most at need are being fed over the holidays, they also give fun and enriching opportunities too.
“For working families, the clubs also offer childcare support, which we all know is much needed during the longer school holiday.”
At Easter, Essex ActivAte ran 224 activity clubs across Essex and Thurrock. Almost 7000 children benefitted, including over 1200 children with SEND needs. For more information on eligibility, booking and session availability, visit the Essex ActivAte website.

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex ActivAte Marks Another Successful Half Term
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Celebrating another successful delivery of its Essex ActivAte half term programme, supporting children, young people and families across Essex with free enriching activities and nutritious meals. Funded by Essex County Council, the half‑term clubs run during the smaller school breaks in February, May and October, providing 2–3 days of high‑quality support for those who need it most.
In 2025, Essex ActivAte delivered significant impact, with 15,050 attendees across all three half terms, and 13,728 funded spaces provided across the three holiday periods. These figures highlight the ongoing demand for accessible, high quality holiday provision for families under financial pressure.
Essex ActivAte clubs are delivered by a trusted network of local providers and run Monday to Friday (unless specified). They offer children an engaging mix of physical activity, enrichment sessions and fun food education. The programme prioritises children eligible for income‑related free school meals and those from low‑income working families, as well as young people who may be vulnerable to inactivity or social isolation without access to this vital support.
For many families, school holidays can be a challenging time. Essex ActivAte clubs give children a safe, welcoming environment to stay active, try new experiences, socialise and enjoy a nutritious meal, while also offering much needed respite for parents and carers. Clubs play a crucial role in supporting children’s physical and mental wellbeing, ensuring they have opportunities to move, learn and build confidence during school breaks.
Local providers and parents continue to emphasise just how essential this support is:
“Children feel accepted and welcomed in our non‑judgemental environment, and parents and carers really value having a couple of hours’ respite. Local SEND provision like this is vital for families and the wider community.” -Provider from Chelmsford
“Thank you so much for the free activities, my girls had an amazing time, you’ve literally saved me to be honest with you! Money can be really tight sometimes.” -Parent from Tendring
With many households experiencing increased cost‑of‑living pressures, free holiday programmes like Essex ActivAte are more important than ever. Not only do they relieve financial strain, but they also ensure that children across Essex have access to high‑quality, meaningful experiences that support both learning and wellbeing.
For more information about the programme and future club dates, visit the Essex ActivAte website.

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex Sporting Stars Rally Behind Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind Campaign
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
In July last year, Active Essex were thrilled to announce an extension of their Find Your Active campaign, Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind.
Powered by Essex Public Health Find Your Active: Move For Your Mind brings about a new chapter from the successful Find Your Active campaign; a county-wide movement, inspiring people of all ages and abilities across the County to discover and enjoy ways to get moving – whether that be getting out in the garden, a short walk, social bike ride or a friendly game of football. It celebrates the fact that everyone can enjoy the huge benefits of moving more, it’s just about finding what’s right for you.
And in January, the campaign made more exciting strides as it launched a new partnership with Mind in Essex, to champion the powerful connection between physical activity and mental wellbeing. The partnership aims to create more opportunities for people across Essex to explore movement in ways that feel enjoyable and accessible.
As the campaign continues to gain momentum, we’re pleased to welcome Paris 2024 Bronze Medal winner, and professional boxer – Lewis Richardson, and British Para Swimmer and World Champion – Ellie Challis into the Active Essex family as our Athlete Ambassador’s for 2026.
Lewis, spent 2025 as our Athlete Ambassador, visiting his old school to deliver an inspiring talk and lead a boxing session, spoke with our Director, Jason Fergus in an interview for International Olympic day. He also helped us task the county with getting active during National School Sports Week and on National Fitness Day. His passion when sharing his story, and his dedication to inspiring the next generation truly inspired us as he went above and beyond in his role as an advocate for Active Essex.
Lewis has had a breakthrough year since the Paris 2024 games where he was the only Team GB boxer to medal, and after a stellar amateur career which led him to Olympic Bronze, has now turned pro. Since making the move to professional boxing, with his debut bout taking place at Ipswich Town’s Portman Road stadium, Lewis has taken part in two fights, finishing as winner in both. He explained;
I’m really excited to be an athlete ambassador for the Find Your Active: Move for Your Mind campaign. Movement has always been a huge part of my life, whether that’s for performance-related purposes or just staying active day to day. Mental strength is really important to me, and I’ve felt first-hand how much better I am mentally when I’m able to move. I’ve also seen the positive impact it’s had on the people around me, it can be a snowball effect, but it all starts with moving.
Ellie is one of Britain’s most decorated young para-swimmers, with a host of Paralympic and World Championship medals to her name, Ellie is also a record breaker, holding the Women’s SB2 50m Breaststroke world record. Ellie’s early-life adversity is well known, she contracted meningitis at 16 months old, resulting in amputations of both legs above the knee and both arms below the elbow.
Despite this, she has forged a remarkable sporting career, regularly sharing her message of resilience, determination, and overcoming barriers. Ellie is also an ambassador for the Meningitis Trust and has been in the role since the age of 5. As an ambassador for the charity, she helps other children adjust to life after limb loss. A previous winner of the Young Sports Personality of the Year award, Ellie has achieved so much at just the age of 21.
“I’m really excited to be working with Active Essex on their Find Your Active Move Your Mind campaign this year. Movement is super important to me because it made physio fun and I met so many friends through being active and swimming. I love seeing people try new sports and ways to be active whilst also having fun.”

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Unlocking community strength
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Active Essex and community partners strengthen voluntary sector organisations, through place-based support
Active Essex, working alongside community partners through Essex County Council’s Your Essex Community programme is accelerating efforts to build the capability and resilience of voluntary and community organisations across the county.
The place-based support offer is ensuring that local groups have the tools, skills and resources they need to meet the diverse needs of residents. By bringing organisations together, the programme is creating the conditions for stronger collaboration, shared learning and greater collective impact.
Community aspirations are being reflected across the place-based module through local training opportunities, peer learning events, and bespoke development support. Recognising that no two places in Essex are the same, Active Essex has worked closely with partners to understand where unmet support needs exist and how we can work together to build resilience and capacity in local voluntary sector organisations. This approach is uncovering deeper insights into local challenges, while helping remove barriers that often limit organisational growth.
Louise Voyce, Active Essex Relationship Development Lead, said:
“We’re proud to support this work and we aim to help build a thriving, connected and resilient sector that meets the needs of local communities.
Based on initial research from 138 voluntary community sector organisations, plus a series of listening exercises, we found that the biggest unmet support needs for the sector were sustainable income generation, access to free and low-cost training, help creating new partnerships and building networks and volunteer recruitment and capacity.
By working with local community organisations and Active Essex partners, we have already been able to excel in providing support to the sector and the impact we’ve seen over the past 6 months, has been great.”
To date, 94% of delegates that have participated in a Your Essex Community place-based support offer, have rated their experience as very satisfied with 82% stating they gained key takeaways that they could apply directly into their work. Similarly, over 100 individuals attended fundraising and small grant workshops learning how to write stronger applications, maximise awarded funding and strengthening governance and organisational confidence.
One participant from North Essex shared:
“It made me realise the number of options to apply for. It gave me focus and clarity on our next steps for applying for funding.”
Active Essex’s commitment to strengthening the voluntary community sector continues. As the organisation moves into 2026, further opportunities will be developed as part of this programme. These include Meet the Funder events, large grant workshops and sessions on partnership building and long-term sustainability.
For more information on the place-based offer and the Your Essex Community initiative, or to apply to deliver infrastructure support for the next phase of programme visit:  www.activeessex.org/your-essex-community/

https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.title: Essex responds to mental health crisis with new movement-focused partnership
https://www.activeessex.org/feed/.text:
Find Your Active: Move for your Mind joins forces with Mind in Essex to help residents discover the powerful link between physical activity and better mental health.
Today (19 January), a new partnership launches in Essex to help residents improve their mental wellbeing by increasing their physical activity. Find Your Active: Move for your Mind and Mind in Essex unite trusted mental health expertise with a county‑wide drive to make movement enjoyable, accessible, and achievable for all.
The Find Your Active campaign, by Active Essex, first launched five years ago to help residents move more following the pandemic. This next phase, powered by Essex Public Health and delivered in partnership with Mind in Essex, focuses specifically on the mental wellbeing benefits of physical activity and aims to support people to take small, achievable steps that make a meaningful difference.
Mind in Essex is a network of local mental‑health charities working across the county to support people experiencing emotional or psychological difficulties. It brings together several independent Mind organisations – Mind in West Essex, Basildon Mind, South East and Central Essex Mind, Mid and North East Essex Mind, and Thurrock and Brentwood Mind – to create a more joined‑up, accessible system of support. Their shared aim is to make it easier for people to find help close to home, reduce stigma around mental health, and offer services ranging from counselling and crisis support to community groups and training, strengthening mental‑health provision for communities throughout Essex.
Through the partnership, residents will benefit from:
Guidance and resources on how movement can support mental wellbeing
Opportunities to join gentle, beginner‑friendly or community‑based activity sessions
Support from local Find Your Active Place Navigators and Mind in Essex ambassadors
Signposting to mental wellbeing activities and services across the county
With 1 in 10 adults and 1 in 6 children in Essex experiencing a mental health problem each year, the partnership arrives at an important time. Research shows that even 10 minutes of movement can lift mood, reduce stress, and build emotional resilience.
Cllr John Spence, Essex County Council Cabinet Member for Children’s Services, Adult Social Care, Public Health and Integration said: “Physical activity isn’t just about physical health, its positive impact on mental wellbeing is clear. Moving in any form refreshes the mind as well as the body. The Move for your Mind addition to the already successful Find Your Active campaign highlights how vital activity is for those facing mental health challenges. I encourage all residents to explore and find the activity that works for them.”
David Sollis, CEO of South East and Central Essex Mind, commented: “We are delighted to be partnering with Find Your Active: Move for your Mind. By combining our mental health expertise with their commitment to accessible activity, we hope to empower more people across Essex to discover movement that supports their wellbeing. This partnership will help us reach individuals who may be struggling and offer them practical, meaningful ways to feel better.”
The Find Your Active campaign partnership will continue throughout 2026, to expand opportunities, strengthen community support, and promote the role of movement in maintaining good mental health.
For more information on the partnership, to explore local activity opportunities, or to access mental wellbeing support, visit: www.activeessex.org/find-your-active
