https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.title: Niki’s Story
https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.text:
Niki's Story: "You Know Your Body Better Than Anyone, Listen To It"
Meet Niki
Niki, an inspiring woman, a mother, a partner, and a Helen Rollason Cancer Charity client. Niki wants to make a difference; she wants to share her story, empower women to stand their ground, feel confident, and not be dismissed.
Listening to Her Body
During 2020, the year of the pandemic, after self-examination Niki found a lump. She was promptly sent to the cancer unit. Fortunately, it was found to be a cyst. Niki was able to relax in the comfort that she had done the right thing in being checked and given the all clear.
Niki continued to be extremely careful and vigilant, regularly putting time into checking her body for any symptoms or signs.
In 2022, again, she found lumps in her breast. She was sent to the cancer unit for a scan for a second time; these too were cysts and she was told that it was all linked to her menstrual cycle.
The Third Visit Changed Everything
Nine months later, in 2023, her journey with cancer began.
Again, Niki found a lump. Feeling awkward, nervous and as if she was wasting the doctors’ time, Niki went to her local GP surgery and, through this visit, she received her referral.
This was the third time within three years that Niki had been to the cancer unit. She felt comfortable enough to go alone, unaware of what she was about to find out and how she was going to be made to feel.
The consultant made her aware that he would not be allowing for a second mammogram to be done within one year. Following this initial uncomfortable meeting came the scan, after which a very different feeling flooded into the room. The atmosphere had shifted; this wasn’t like the first two times.
Niki was then sent for a biopsy and a mammogram. Left feeling anxious, all she could do was go back to her car. She was alone.
Niki describes the wait for the results as traumatic and an out-of-body experience; it is something that cannot escape your mind, even for a minute.
Then it happened.
She heard the news nobody wants to hear – it’s cancer.
A Diagnosis with Further Challenges
Once on the path, Niki cannot sing her praises of the NHS loud enough.
Unfortunately, her biopsy could not provide clear answers. The clinical team were still unsure as to what type of cancer it was and needed to seek a second opinion.
A plan was put into place promptly. Niki was to have a lumpectomy, followed by six months of chemotherapy, after which she would undergo radiotherapy.
However, the answers from her biopsy were frightening. The cancer was triple negative, which was the worst outcome for Niki.
Genetic testing then confirmed a mutation in the ATM gene. All plans had to be changed. She now needed to undergo a double mastectomy without radiotherapy; this was to prevent further breast cancer, as a future diagnosis would have been extremely likely.
Reconstruction and Recovery
At the beginning of 2024, Niki’s reconstruction took place.
The surgery went well; however, she sadly contracted an infection which the medical team described as borderline sepsis.
What was already an incredibly scary time was turning into Niki’s worst nightmare, with obstacle after obstacle. Niki had to focus on all her mental strength to get through this worrisome time.
Cancer patients tend to feel as if they have lost who they are during this time, bewildered and overcome. They are on a journey no one wishes to face; fast-paced, full of language they may not understand, and full of confusion around making decisions that need to be made frightfully quickly.
A Mother’s Concern
Despite all Niki was going through, like all parents, her focus was on her daughter.
What do the implications of her diagnosis mean for her?
For herself there was no family history available, as she had been adopted as a child. But for her daughter, Niki wanted answers.
Her daughter, aged 27, was also positive for the ATM gene, which means there is a significant increase in the risk of her having breast cancer in the future

https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.title: Elaine’s Story
https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.text:
Elaine is 79 and lives in Witham with her husband Simon. She was diagnosed with cancer in 2023 and came to our Centre for the first time when she finished her treatment. For Elaine, HRCC has truly been a lifeline. This is her story.
How HRCC Has Helped
Helen Rollason Cancer Charity has helped me so much.  It’s not easy to put into words the difference it has made to my life. They help me to adapt my routines and always give me so much comfort, both physically and mentally.
I love visiting the Centre, and I’ve seen first-hand the true value that your donation will bring. When you support our charity, you are helping to heal those with cancer, which also brings relief to their families and loved ones.
Hearing I Was Clear of Cancer
In September 2023 my oncologist told me that I was clear of cancer, and I asked him to repeat that several times as it was so difficult to believe. I know that my cancer is not curable and may return.
They told me to go out and live my life, and they would be monitoring me with three-monthly checkups and regular scans.
Trying to Find Normality Again
All any of us really want is to live a normal life again: – as we know it. We don’t want or need a lot: just to regain the normality and stability that we used to know.  But you can’t do this on your own.  When everything shifts out of your control for any length of time, you may need help to find your way back to your version of normality.  Whilst you are following a strict medical regime of cancer treatment, you are not in control, you are in the hands of many others – for weeks, months or maybe even years. But once your treatment ends, it’s almost like you have to try and find your life again.  You can feel lost, and wonder `What do I do now?”
Reaching Out for Support
I remember the nurses at the hospital advising me to go to Helen Rollason Cancer Charity for support, but whilst going through treatment I was just totally focused on getting through each day at a time. I only looked into it when my treatment finished, and I was trying to find my way back to my life.  So, I called the number, and we had a chat, and then they told me to come in; so that we could find the way forward together.
Therapies That Helped Me
Today, I still come in for reflexology, and I’ve also had counselling and taken part in group mindfulness, which are all amazing therapies. Because the chemotherapy has left me with lymphoedema in my left leg, the Centre also helps me with regular manual lymphatic drainage. This has helped me maintain a healthy routine to reduce swelling, and to better understand the lymphatic system, of which I knew nothing before. Most recently, I have also received yoga therapy for lymphoedema, which involved group sessions and has been really enjoyable and informative.
A Place Where I Feel I Belong
We are all so different, and our cancer experiences and the routes we travel are also extremely varied. Cancer impacts on you whoever you are, both physically and mentally, and turns your world upside down.   But when you walk into the Centre, a feeling  of calm, euphoric trust comes over you, and I even feel as though I want to hug everyone for just ‘being there’ for me and for helping me regain my strength in both my mind and my body.
It’s probably a different feeling or experience for everyone, but for me this is somewhere special that we all have a place, and we all belong. Life feels OK again, It’s like a club!
Feeling Safe and Understood
When you come in, you can finally start to relax and be yourself. Your mind starts to ease, bringing you back to being able to experience all the joy that life can offer.  Coming to the Centre feels like being in a cocoon; as you feel safe and you can shut out the world for a while and just be yourself. You can talk about anything, as this is the one place where you don’t have to put on a brave face.
Our charity provides an environment of comfort and safety. All the therapies and treatments are holistic, and the therapists a

https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.title: A Ride With Purpose: Graeme’s Story of Resilience and Recovery
https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.text:
A Decade of Ride For Helen – and a Personal Milestone
Graeme’s story
In 2024 Graeme joined Helen Rollason Cancer Charity’s cycle ride – the popular ‘Ride For Helen’ which was in its 10 th year.  At the age of 50, Graeme cycled 50 miles in 3 hours and 41 minutes and raised over £2,800 for the charity.  Each year hundreds of cyclists join Ride For Helen and pedal through the Essex countryside raising money for the charity.
However, for Graeme it was a challenge in 2024.  He had throat cancer and, just a few days after the cycle event, he underwent surgery.  He continues to support Helen Rollason Cancer Charity and in 2025 he pushed himself further and cycled the 65 miles route. Graeme is still undergoing monitoring for cancer but he is determined to keep cycling and maintain his health.
Why I Ride – In Graeme’s Words
Graeme told us:
“I have taken part in the Ride For Helen events for a number of years – sometimes with family and at other times on my own.  These events give me a goal to train for.  I need a reason to get out and cycle, which in turn improves my physical and mental health.
When I started out, I would choose the lower mileage cycle routes and I worked up to being comfortable with 30 miles.  This was enough to be challenging without causing too much recovery post-event.
For 2024 I wanted to push myself out of my comfort zone and tackle the 50 miles event.  I also turned 50 that year – on the same day as Ride For Helen – so there was no question really.  I also received my second cancer diagnosis at the start of 2024 and had surgery two days after the cycle event.  Doing the event in 2024 was really important to me and certainly helped with my mental preparedness too.
The Link Between Physical and Mental Health
I firmly believe that, in the same way you may choose to exercise to improve your physical well-being, you also need to work hard to maintain a healthy mental well-being.  Having one without the other can only provide half of the benefit.  Helen Rollason is, in my view, there to offer the support and provide the ‘mental scaffolding’ for people when they need it most.  In the same way that health care services look to treat the cancer, the services provided by Helen Rollason treat and support mental health aspects such as reducing anxiety through reassurance and providing a safe environment to focus on “you”.
A Calm Space to Heal and Reflect
The need for the services provided by Helen Rollason is increasing with more people being diagnosed with cancer and at younger ages.  The more people are aware of what Helen Rollason Cancer Charity has to offer, the greater the benefits their services can provide.
Walking into the centre in Hatfield Peverel feels like leaving the busy day-to-day at the door – it is a calm and peaceful environment.  I was surprised at the number of privacy-respecting treatment rooms that are available, all maintained to a high standard.  As well as specific treatment spaces there is a lovely outdoor garden and seating area for more informal chats.  Having a facility like this is a real asset.
Looking Ahead: What’s Next for Graeme?
I plan to continue to support Helen Rollason in the future by continuing with the Ride For Helen annual cycle events.  I was very lucky in 2024 in having so many generous supporters who donated such an amazing amount to help with the costs of such a worthwhile and well needed local facility.
“I may not wait until I am 100 to take on the challenge of the 100 miles route though!”
Ride for Helen 2026
Inspired by Graeme’s story? Join hundreds of cyclists and take part in the next Ride For Helen – whether it’s 6 miles or 100, every pedal stroke helps support people living with cancer.

https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.title: In Memory of Ed Knight: Honouring a Cycling Enthusiast and Beloved Supporter
https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.text:
Following our earlier acknowledgment, we would now like to share that Helen Rollason Cancer Charity sadly lost one of our greatest supporters at the Ride for Helen cycling event this month, Ed Knight. Ed had supported Helen Rollason Cancer Charity since 2017 helping us to be there for those living with cancer and their loved ones.
Andrew Watson, his “partner in crime”, shares Ed’s story.
Ed Knight, an enthusiastic, and knowledgeable vintage bicycle rider, with an infectious grin, and boundless energy brought a whole new dimension to the Ride for Helen event. In 2017 he turned up with his “ordinary bicycle” more commonly known today as a “Penny Farthing”.
The bemused faces of the onlookers turned to incredulity as three more riders crossed the start line on their machines with front wheels measuring anything from 48 to 54 inches high.
The following year Ed arrived with an eclectic mix of men, women, and children all riding penny farthings. They completed the 15-mile route arriving back at The Crix to sign out, only to shoot off around the house to do the six-mile route just so that they could stop at Paper Mill Lock for a spot of lunch!
Every year since then, Ed Knight has turned up in the company of fellow vintage bicycle enthusiasts on an array of beguiling machines. The firm crowd favourite, however, remained the towering Penny Farthings. Anyone who showed an interest could suddenly find themselves clambering up to the saddle under the patient guidance of Ed, whilst trying not to look terrified as they posed for a photo with their head 9 feet off the ground. The more daring would then find themselves being given their very first lesson in riding a Penny Farthing as Ed encouraged a quick go behind the start line.
Ed had a deep knowledge and understanding of the development of the bicycle, and would soon be involved in an engaging explanation with those who wanted to know more.
Over the years, Ed had ridden his bikes throughout the UK and Europe including a Penny Farthing ride from Paris to London. Everyone who met him soon became firm friends and a short acquaintance would feel like a friendship of years, he just seemed to find time for everyone.
A true gentleman of the cycling world, he was intrigued by the often-ingenious creations of the early bicycle pioneers and if he couldn’t find an existing example, as a gifted engineer he would make his own.
When ride for Helen Suffolk was created, Ed took his Victorian bicycle collection to display at the start line. He set off on several occasions on various machines never getting more than a few hundred yards, much to the amusement of the other riders.
Once again, this year Ed set off from The Crix on his Penny Farthing, smiling and waving as he rolled down the drive towards the exit. He had a great ride with his companions, heading off the beaten track for tea and cake, before finally re-joining the route to head back towards Hatfield Peverel.
Suddenly, without warning, he collapsed and despite immediate help from his friends, passers-by and the quick response of the emergency services, Ed passed away at the scene doing the thing he loved….cycling.
We at Helen Rollason Cancer Charity will miss such a gregarious and knowledgeable gentleman.  Ed was, and will remain, part of the Helen Rollason Cancer Charity family. In his honour the 15mile route will now and forever more be known as Ed’s Route; granting all cyclists the opportunity to ride, eat cake and smile in his memory.
Edwin leaves behind his wife Mary, his daughter Claire, son in law Tony and two grandchildren, Ayrton and Ila.
If you feel you would like to donate to the Helen Rollason Cancer Charity in Ed’s memory, or leave a message of condolences, please do so below. We will share all your kind words with his family.

https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.title: A success for Christmas tree recycling 2024
https://www.helenrollason.org.uk/feed/.text:
Over the first weekend of January, a team of volunteers met at the Helen Rollason Cancer Charity centre in Hatfield Peverel, Essex. Fuelled by tea and bacon rolls, they set off around Essex to collect Christmas trees from residents in exchange for a donation to the charity. The trees were then delivered to sites around Essex where they were shredded and recycled. Almost 800 trees were collected, and around £15,000 was raised for the charity. This money will be used to help support local people living with cancer.
Head of Fundraising, Zoe Jay, said:
“It was a great achievement. We would like to thank everyone who gave a donation and the amazing volunteers and local businesses that supported us. More than 20 vans were collecting around Essex, and we are so grateful to those that volunteered as drivers and helpers to pick up the trees. We would also like to thank the local businesses that supported us including Beachenlea for shredding the trees, Amazon, Group 1 Audi, Herd Hire, Group 1 Volkswagen and Just Wheels for providing vans, New Hall School, Museum of Power, and Marsh Farm for use of their sites.”
Statement from Group 1 Volkswagen, Headline Sponsor:
Darren Thompson, Franchise Director said “Here at Group 1 Volkswagen, we have a long-standing relationship with the Helen Rollason Cancer Charity and have supported a number of events and sponsorships. The Christmas Tree Recycling Campaign is another great example of working in and around the local community to help raise money for a good cause, in which we are delighted to be a part.”
Statement from Marsh Farm, Supporting Partner:
Aaron said “We wanted to support Helen Rollason Cancer Charity as it’s a local charity that does amazing work within the community with people affected by cancer. We wanted to support this program and boost awareness especially over the festive period.”
The Fundraising Team is now turning their attention to future events, including the popular Ride For Helen cycle ride, Rural Ramble, Open Gardens, and the summer Vintage Fairs. Keep your eyes on the Helen Rollason Cancer Charity website for details of events.
The charity supports men and women with all types of cancer at all stages. Information on the types of support offered can be found on their website.

https://affc.org.uk/feed/.title: Celebrating our long-service volunteers with a special Tiptree treat
https://affc.org.uk/feed/.text:
At Action for Family Carers, our volunteers make a real difference to the lives of unpaid carers and the people they support. We’re proud to celebrate their dedication and grateful to Essex-based business Wilkin & Sons, makers of the famous Tiptree Jams, for recognising our long-service volunteers with a special treat.
The family business generously donated gift vouchers for our volunteers to enjoy at its Tiptree Tea Rooms. We invited three of our long-standing volunteers to join us at our Annual General Meeting (AGM), where we recognised their incredible commitment to the charity.
Between them, Pat, Angela and Alison have dedicated an amazing 24 years of service to supporting people across Essex.
Making a difference through volunteering
Pat and Angela have volunteered at our Maldon Day Centre for more than 16 years between them, helping us provide a welcoming and supportive environment for older people, including those living with dementia and memory loss.
Pat shared what volunteering means to her:
“Volunteering at the day centre can be challenging, as some of our clients have dementia and memory loss, but the gratitude I feel from their loved ones makes it all worthwhile. I can see it in their faces when they drop off or pick up. They know the person they care for will be safe.”
Pat’s words highlight the difference volunteers make, not only to the people they spend time with, but also to the families who rely on our services. Knowing a loved one is safe, cared for and enjoying their time at the day centre can give family carers valuable peace of mind.
Alison has also made a lasting contribution, volunteering as a befriender for nine years. By offering companionship and a friendly face, she helps people feel less alone and reminds us how even small acts of kindness can have a lasting impact.
Thank you to Wilkin & Sons
We were delighted to welcome Liz from Wilkin & Sons to our AGM to present the gift vouchers and help us celebrate our volunteers’ dedication.
This thoughtful initiative will recognise all Action for Family Carers volunteers who have given more than three years of service to the charity. We hope the vouchers provide a well-deserved opportunity to relax and enjoy a treat at the Tiptree Tea Rooms .
We’re incredibly grateful to Wilkin & Sons for supporting this initiative and, above all, proud of the many dedicated volunteers who work alongside our staff across our services.
Could you volunteer with Action for Family Carers?
Volunteering is a rewarding way to make a difference in your local community. Whether you have a little time to spare or want to make a regular commitment, there are opportunities to suit different interests and availability.
Our volunteers support people in many ways, including helping at young carer clubs, welcoming people at carer support groups and making someone feel at home over a cup of tea.
You don’t need to change the world in a day. Sometimes, simply being there for someone can make all the difference.
Find out more about our current opportunities and how you could help support unpaid carers and their families.

At our Maldon Day Centre, we are always looking for new ways to keep the people we support active, entertained and engaged .
We also look for ways to make life a little easier for our staff and volunteers, giving them more time to talk to, listen to and support our clients.
And we are not afraid to try something new!
Bringing a little magic to the day
Thanks to some generous funding, we have been able to get a Magic Table from Social-Ability through its Happiness Programme.
The Magic Table uses interactive light technology to provide a range of games and sensory activities, designed for people living with cognitive and physical disabilities.
And it has already been a big hit!
Our clients, staff and volunteers have all given it a big thumbs up. 👍
With lots of different games and activities to choose from, we can use it with smaller groups and give everyone the chance to get involved. Best of all, it can be used whatever the weather!
More time for what matters
The Magic Table is another way for our team to bring people together, encourage interaction and provide meaningful activities.
It is also a great example of the thought and care our Maldon Day Centre team puts into making each day enjoyable for the people we support.
Supporting carers too
Our Day Centre gives unpaid carers a safe and trusted place to bring the person they care for, knowing they will be well looked after.
This gives carers time to work, attend appointments, take a break or simply have some time for themselves , knowing their loved one is enjoying their day too.
When we support the person being cared for, we support the carer too.

1-7th November 2026
Befriending Week 1–7 November 2026
Befriending Week celebrates the positive impact of befriending in reducing loneliness, strengthening communities, and recognising the dedication of volunteers and the difference they make to people’s lives across the UK.
At Support 4 Sight, we offer a friendly telephone befriending service for people who may be feeling lonely or at risk of isolation. Regular calls are made to those who have expressed an interest in hearing from someone, providing a listening ear, a friendly chat, and a meaningful connection.
Between January and September this year, our visually impaired befrienders made 777 befriending calls, helping people feel more connected and supported.
The impact of our service is reflected in the kind words we receive from those who use it:
‘Your calls are a lifeline to me as I don’t see anyone else and really appreciate them’
‘Its really nice to know someone cares and calls regularly for befriending calls. Thank you for setting this up.’
These comments highlight just how much a regular phone call can mean to someone who may otherwise feel isolated. We are incredibly grateful to our befrienders for giving their time, sharing a friendly conversation, and helping make a real difference to people’s lives.

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: Give a Little Love this GivingTuesday
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Tuesday 1 December 2026 is GivingTuesday, a global day of giving that encourages people to support the charities and causes that matter to them.
Following the excitement of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, GivingTuesday offers a welcome opportunity to think about giving back. Whether it’s donating to your favourite charity, volunteering your time or simply helping to spread the word, it’s about recognising the difference we can make when we support others.
At Remus Horse Sanctuary, every little bit of support makes a difference to the lives of more than 100 rescued horses, ponies and donkeys.
Rescue is just the beginning. Providing a safe home for an animal who may have experienced neglect, abandonment or difficult circumstances means a lifetime commitment to their care. There’s food, bedding, shelter, veterinary treatment and all the everyday attention that helps each animal feel safe, comfortable and loved.
As a charity that receives no government funding, Remus relies on the generosity of its supporters to continue this work. And right now, one of our biggest ongoing costs is feeding our residents .
The prolonged drought in the summer has made sourcing hay more challenging, while prices have risen considerably. With around nine large bales needed every week, the cost of keeping everyone fed quickly adds up.
Thanks to the incredible generosity of our supporters, we’ve already raised more than £2,500 through our hay appeal. But the cost of feeding more than 100 rescued horses, ponies and donkeys hasn’t gone away. With hay costing around £5,400 a month, every donation helps us meet this essential ongoing expense and keep our residents fed and cared for.
This GivingTuesday, why not give a little love to Remus by supporting our hay appeal?
Every donation , however large or small, will help us meet the cost of feeding our rescued residents and ensuring they continue to receive the care they deserve.
If you’re able to make a donation, we’d be incredibly grateful. And if donating isn’t possible, sharing our appeal with your friends, family or on social media is another valuable way to help.
Support our hay appeal today .
Every act of kindness counts. Thank you for being part of the Remus family.
#GivingTuesday #GivingTuesdayUK #TogetherTuesday #GetInspired

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: Meet the Twelve Stars of the Remus 2027 Calendar
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
There are plenty of familiar faces at Remus Horse Sanctuary, but have you met the twelve special characters starring in our 2027 wall calendar?
From Brian in January to Stix in December, each month features a different animal, all with their own story and place in the Remus family.
Whether you’re a regular visitor to the Sanctuary or follow our work from further afield, we hope you’ll enjoy getting to know the animals who will be keeping you company throughout 2027!
January – Brian
We start the year with Brian, a rather cheeky goat who certainly knows how to make an impression!
Brian arrived at Remus in October 2022 after being found wandering loose on an industrial estate. Thankfully, a concerned member of the public, who happened to be a neighbour of the Sanctuary, brought him to our attention.
He’s settled in beautifully and loves showing off when visitors approach his fence, usually with a few enthusiastic headbutts! He spends his days enjoying the paddocks with his friends Patrick, Peppa and Rocky.
February – Smudge
February belongs to Smudge, one of several cats rescued from the East End when the Olympic sites were being developed.
Smudge and his littermates had a terrible start in life, living in awful conditions without proper food or care. Thankfully, they were rescued and brought to Remus, where they’ve been able to enjoy the safe and comfortable lives they deserve.
Now eight years old, Smudge needs medication for urinary problems resulting from his early neglect. But that doesn’t stop him enjoying his daily routine of breakfast, playtime, lunch and a cosy afternoon nap. He’s also rather thoughtful, sometimes seeking out poorly sheep, horses or goats to sit with and offer a little comfort.
March – Hovis
Our March star is Hovis, a donkey who came to Remus after his owners moved to Wales.
Sadly, the horse he was living with was picking on him, and the situation had been reported to the RSPCA several times. Things came to a head during the journey to Wales when the horse attacked Hovis. On arrival, the people taking the animals in refused to accept him.
Hovis was forced to make the journey back to Essex, leaving his transporters with a donkey and nowhere to take him. Remus stepped in and offered him a home.
Today, Hovis enjoys life with his donkey friends and is particularly protective of Wesley and Spencer.
He’s certainly found his place in the herd!
Find out more about sponsoring Hovis .
April – Clementine
Meet Clementine, our lovely little Shetland pony.
Clementine arrived at Remus in 2012 with her friend Cassie after the petting farm where they lived closed down. Sadly, Cassie passed away a few years ago, but Clementine continues to enjoy life at the Sanctuary.
Now 33 years old, she’s a sweet-natured but rather nervous pony who prefers her own company. She also has Cushing’s Disease and Equine Metabolic Syndrome, which means her diet and daily care need careful management.
She’s a lovely reminder that every animal deserves a safe and happy retirement, whatever their age or needs.
May – Mason
May features Mason, whose rescue story is a powerful reminder of just how much animals can care for one another.
When Mason was just three months old, he and two other youngsters, Heidi and Alfie, were found chained to the ground by their necks. Remus managed to rescue all three, but little Alfie was already desperately poorly. Sadly, he died within days, despite our best efforts to save him.
Footage from the Sanctuary’s cameras showed something incredibly moving. When Alfie sat down, Mason left his hay and went to sit beside his little friend. They then both lay down together. Half an hour later, Mason got up and returned to his hay. In that short time, Alfie had passed away.
Mason and Heidi went on to recover, receiving intensive veterinary care, including twice-daily penicillin injections. Today, Mason enjoys a very different life, free from pain, fear and hunger.
Find out more about sponsoring Mason .
June – Dolly

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: Making a Difference: Affinity Fostering Supports Remus’s Artisan Market
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
There’s something rather special about a community coming together to support a good cause. Whether it’s buying from a local maker, enjoying something delicious, donating to a charity or simply turning up to an event, every contribution can make a difference.
That’s exactly what we’re hoping for when we welcome visitors to our Artisan Market at Stock Village Hall on Sunday 11 October , and we’re delighted to have local fostering agency Affinity Fostering supporting the event as our sponsor.
Taking place from 11am to 4pm, the market will bring together a lovely selection of handmade products and locally produced food, offering visitors the chance to discover some great local makers and producers while helping to raise much-needed funds for the horses, ponies and donkeys in our care.
For Affinity Fostering , supporting local communities is also an important part of what they do.
Based at Ingatestone Hall, the agency supports foster carers across Essex and beyond, with a focus on enhancing and empowering young lives. Affinity has been rated Outstanding by Ofsted and places a strong emphasis on supporting its foster carers, including dedicated social workers, local support groups and 24/7 support.
But fostering is about more than providing a safe and nurturing home. Affinity also aims to create a strong sense of community for its foster families, with family days, activities, support groups and events designed to give children and young people positive experiences and opportunities.
That shared belief in the importance of community makes Affinity a particularly fitting sponsor for our Artisan Market.
Andy Robins, CEO of Affinity EFS Group Ltd and Director & Responsible Individual of Affinity Fostering Services Ltd, said:
“We’re delighted to be supporting the Remus Horse Sanctuary Artisan Market. At Affinity Fostering, community is incredibly important to us, and we’re always keen to support local organisations and events that bring people and families together. Remus does fantastic work, and sponsoring the Artisan Market is a great opportunity for us to support a worthwhile local cause while being part of what should be a brilliant community event.”
If you’ve ever wondered whether fostering could be right for you, the Artisan Market could also be an opportunity to find out a little more about Affinity and the difference you could make to a young person’s life.
You don’t need to know whether fostering is definitely right for you before getting in touch. Affinity’s friendly team can answer your questions, explain what fostering involves and talk you through the process without any obligation.
As Affinity says, foster carers come from all sorts of backgrounds. What matters most is having the time, stability and commitment to provide a safe and nurturing home for a child who needs one.
To find out more about fostering with Affinity, call 01245 237158 or visit www.affinityfostering.com .
We’re delighted to have Affinity Fostering supporting this event, and hope this will be the start of a positive relationship. We’re always grateful to businesses that want to support Remus, whether through event sponsorship, fundraising or other opportunities to get involved. To find out more, please contact Alison via email to: funding@remussanctuary.org .
And, of course, we’d love to see you at the Remus Artisan Market on Sunday 11 October . Come along, enjoy the market, support our local makers and help us raise funds for the animals at Remus Horse Sanctuary.
Sunday 11 October 2026 | 11am–4pm
Stock Village Hall, Common Road, Stock CM4 9NF
We look forward to seeing you there!

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: Remus Horse Sanctuary to celebrate World Animal Day at final Open Day of 2026
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Remus Horse Sanctuary will be opening its gates for the final Open Day of 2026 on Sunday 4 October from 1pm to 4pm, giving visitors one last opportunity this year to meet the Sanctuary’s beautiful rescue animals and learn more about the work that goes on behind the scenes. The event also coincides with World Animal Day, making it a particularly special day for everyone at Remus and the animals in its care.
World Animal Day is celebrated around the world every year on 4 October, raising awareness of animal welfare and encouraging people to take action to improve the lives of animals. For Remus, which provides a safe and loving home for more than 100 rescued horses, ponies, donkeys and other animals, it’s a fitting occasion to celebrate the animals who have found their way to the Sanctuary and the people who help make their continued care possible.
Visitors to the October Open Day will be able to meet many of the animals, find out more about their individual stories and see first-hand how Remus cares for its residents throughout the year. There will also be a range of stalls and activities to enjoy, making it a lovely day out for animal lovers of all ages. As the final Open Day of the year, it’s also a chance to say goodbye to the Sanctuary until the Open Days return in 2027, while continuing to support the vital work of the charity.
Sue Burton, Founder of Remus Horse Sanctuary, said: “It feels particularly fitting that our final Open Day of 2026 falls on World Animal Day. Every day at Remus is about putting the animals first, giving them the care, kindness and safe home they deserve.
“Our Open Days give people the opportunity to meet some of the animals, hear their stories and see why our work is so important. We’d love to welcome everyone to the Sanctuary on 4 October for what promises to be a very special day, and to celebrate the wonderful animals who are at the heart of everything we do.”
To find out more and book your tickets in advance, please visit the Sanctuary’s website at: www.remussanctuary.org/events/open-day-sanctuary-october/ or tel: 01277 356191.

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: September Birthday Celebrations at Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
September has been a busy month for birthday celebrations here at Remus, with three very special residents reaching another year older.
We may be halfway through the month already, but we couldn’t let September pass without wishing Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty a very happy birthday!
These are also the last of our birthday celebrations for 2026, as we don’t have any animals with birthdays in October, November or December. Of course, that doesn’t mean the celebrations stop. Every animal here at Remus is special to us, and they’re loved, cared for and celebrated every single day.
Happy 20th Birthday Winston!
Winston celebrated his 20th birthday on 4 September .
Winston was found at an illegal Traveller’s sale, standing alone in a dirty trailer hidden around the back. He was extremely thin and totally terrified.
When Winston arrived at Remus, blood tests revealed that he had severe liver problems caused by ragwort poisoning. He’d been kept in a field full of ragwort with nothing else available, so he was forced to eat it.
Thankfully, Winston came through this difficult time and he now thoroughly enjoys his life at Remus, surrounded by the care and companionship he deserves.
If you’d like to sponsor Winston , you can find out more by clicking on the web page with the link.
If you’d like to get Winston a birthday present as well, you can choose something from our animal treats section .
Happy 9th Birthday Marmite 2!
Marmite 2 celebrated his 9th birthday on 6 September .
Marmite had an awful start in life. He and Flint were kept in a cage for much of their early lives and were desperately thin, as well as being full of worms and covered in lice.
Thankfully, their lives are very different now. Marmite and Flint enjoy their freedom here at Remus, living happily with their field mates and receiving the care they need.
If you’d like to get Marmite 2 a birthday present , you can choose something from our animal treats section.
Happy 33rd Birthday Minty!
Minty celebrated his 33rd birthday on 22 September .
Minty came to us with three other ponies from a riding school after the owner and their 12 other horses were evicted. We were able to find homes for 12 of the horses, while the four oldest came into Remus’ care.
These ponies had been much loved and well cared for at the riding school, where they taught many youngsters in Essex how to ride and respect horses. Now Minty enjoys his retirement at Remus with his best friend and fellow riding school pony, Scotty.
Minty unfortunately has breathing problems and, during the summer, needs a respiratory pump with medication to help him breathe more easily. He takes his medication very well, and is well cared for by the Remus team.
Click on the link if you’d like to sponsor Minty .
If you’d also like to get Minty a birthday present, you can choose something from our animal treats section .
Celebrating our Remus residents every day
Birthdays are always a lovely opportunity to celebrate some of the individual characters who make up the Remus family and share a little more of their stories.
But while Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty have had their special birthday treats this month, every day is about giving all of our residents the care, kindness and security they deserve.
We’ll be back with our next birthday celebrations in January, but in the meantime, we’ll continue celebrating our wonderful herd and pack every day.
If you’d like to help us care for the animals at Remus, there are lots of ways you can support the Sanctuary, from sponsoring an animal to choosing a special treat for one of our residents.
If you’d like to meet Winston, Marmite 2 and Minty – and the rest of our darling rescues – our last Open Day of the season will take place on Sunday 4 October .

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: A Lasting Gift for the Future of Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Remember A Charity Week takes place from 7–13 September , providing a timely opportunity to think about the charities and causes that matter to you and how you might continue to support them in the future.
For Remus Horse Sanctuary, the future is something we think about every day.
Our animals rely on us for food, veterinary care, shelter and everything else they need to live happy and healthy lives. With over 100 horses, donkeys and other animals in our care, ensuring that we can continue providing that support for years to come is incredibly important.
One way you can help is by leaving a gift to Remus in your Will.
A gift in your Will, however large or small, can make a lasting difference to the animals at the Sanctuary. It could be a fixed amount, a particular item or asset, or a share of what remains of your estate after other gifts have been made.
There can also be Inheritance Tax benefits to leaving a gift to a registered charity. Charitable gifts are generally exempt from Inheritance Tax, and leaving at least 10% of your net estate to charity may reduce the rate of Inheritance Tax payable on the remainder of your estate. For the most up-to-date information, visit the [ GOV.UK guidance on leaving gifts to charity in your Will ].
Making a Will is a personal decision, and it’s important to make sure it reflects your wishes and circumstances. Remus has partnered with FreeWills , which provides a free Will-writing service, making it simple to put your wishes in writing without the usual cost of a solicitor.
If you already have a Will, it is also worth reviewing it from time to time to make sure it still reflects your wishes.
For Remus, a gift in your Will isn’t simply a donation. It is a way of helping to protect the future of animals who may need a safe home and lifelong care.
If Remus is a charity close to your heart, we would be incredibly grateful if you would consider remembering the Sanctuary in your Will.
Find out more about supporting Remus and leaving a lasting legacy on our website.

https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.title: September Open Day: Come and Meet the Animals at Remus
https://www.remussanctuary.org/feed/.text:
Join us at Remus Horse Sanctuary on Sunday 6 September for our penultimate Open Day of the year. From 1pm to 4pm, you can come and meet our wonderful horses, ponies, donkeys and other rescued animals, explore the Sanctuary, enjoy refreshments and browse the stalls. It’s a lovely afternoon out for all ages, and, importantly, your visit helps to support the vital work we do every day.
This year has been particularly challenging for the Sanctuary, with the ongoing drought putting additional pressure on our fields and meaning we are having to rely more heavily on bought-in hay and other resources to keep our animals well fed. With no government funding, the support we receive from our visitors, donors and supporters really does make a difference.
The dry conditions also mean that the Sanctuary is 100% smoking and vape free . With the fields and surrounding land so dry, the risk of a fire is something we simply cannot take. We ask everyone visiting the Sanctuary to respect this rule and help us keep our animals, team and visitors safe.
So, why not make a date for Sunday 6 September ? Come and meet the animals, enjoy a few hours at the Sanctuary and help support the work we do. And if you can’t make September, our final Open Day of the year is Sunday 4 October .
Book your tickets here >
We look forward to welcoming you!

https://basildon.foodbank.org.uk/feed/.title: Last Year, Basildon Food bank saw the highest ever levels of need
https://basildon.foodbank.org.uk/feed/.text:
On Wednesday 26 April 2023, we released our stats on the number of emergency food parcels that Basildon Food bank provided within our local community between April 2022 and March 2023.
The alarming new figures reveal that we have provided 3,362 emergency food parcels to people who couldn’t afford the essentials in Basildon over the last year – and 1,490 of these went to children.
In addition to this, food banks across the Trussell Trust network provided nearly 3 million (2,986,203) emergency food parcels to people experiencing hunger during this time – with over 1 million of these going to children.
This is the most parcels food banks in our network have ever distributed in a single year and represents a 37% increase compared to last year, and more than double the amount distributed by food banks in the same period five years ago.
This isn’t right and we can’t allow this to go on.
Together, with food banks across the Trussell Trust network, we are calling for MPs across the UK to support a social security system that guarantees our essentials, by making sure that the basic rate of Universal Credit is at least enough to afford the essentials we all need to live.
If you would like to support us by writing to your local MP, please click here to find out more.
No one should need the support of our food bank because everyone in our local community should be able to live lives free from hardship and poverty.
That’s why your support is needed now more than ever.
As we navigate these challenging times and do our utmost to meet the increasing need for our services, we would be most grateful if you could:
Please donate all types of non-perishable food items or toiletries at our usual donation points: Tesco Basildon Extra, Off Station Lane, SS13 3JU, Mayflower Retail Park, Gardiners Link, Basildon, SS14 3HZ, Pitsea Leisure Centre, Northlands Pavement, Basildon, SS13 3DU
Please make a financial donation online: https://app.goodhub.com/offerings/basildon-foodbank-operated-by-rccg-majesty-connections/donations/create , by cheque or in cash at Pitsea Leisure Centre, Northlands Pavement, Basildon, SS13 3DU
For additional support volunteering please contact us at info@basildon.foodbank.org.uk
We recognise how difficult times are right now, which is why we really appreciate all and any support you are able to offer. Together, we can ensure help is here for everyone who needs it in Basildon, whilst we also collectively work towards a more just future where no one needs our food bank to get by.
Thank you for all that you’re doing.

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Ebbsfleet United 1 Billericay Town 1
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Ebbsfleet United 1 (Hessenthaler 13) – Billericay Town 1 (Ruff 4)
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Keith Riley
Charlie Ruff’s early strike helped earn Billericay Town a point away to league leaders Ebbsfleet United, extending their unbeaten league run to 12 matches.
The Blues didn’t have to wait long to get their noses in front when Ruff latched onto Elliot Long’s header before superbly lifting the ball over the diving Will Buse to give his side the lead after just four minutes.
Ebbsfleet responded well and levelled nine minutes later when a deflected cross from the right found Jake Hessenthaler, who took a touch before firing home the equaliser.
The hosts started to dominate play and came close on 17 minutes, when Toby Edser was thwarted by Khari Ranson before Fin Barnes skied the rebound from 12 yards out.
The pressure continued from the home side, and Ranson was needed again on 27 minutes to push Edser’s shot away from danger.
Billericay then thought they may have had a penalty when Merrifield went down at the far post, but despite loud appeals from those in blue, referee Jack Bloxham was unmoved.
Fleet came close twice again in quick succession towards the end of the half, with Louis Lomas making a brilliant interception to deny Dominic Samuel before Ranson caught Ben Chapman’s curling strike, meaning the sides headed into the break level.
Billericay started the second half the brighter and had a golden chance to go in front when Long released Callum Watts through on goal, but the midfielder could only roll his shot wide with only Buse to beat.
Town came close again on 56 minutes when Jon Benton found space in the box but lashed over the bar, with a pass to Merrifield perhaps the better option.
The game opened up as both sides looked for a second, with Ranson again on hand to push away James Vennings’ shot from distance before gratefully gathering Edser’s deflected follow-up.
The visitors responded with a chance of their own as, after good hold-up play from Merrifield, Benton stung the palms of Buse from ten yards on 72 minutes.
Ebbsfleet pushed on for a late winner and saw Ranson intervene again, this time diverting Chapman’s cross into the path of Danny Ogunleye, but the substitute’s shot was brilliantly blocked by Lomas.
Chapman was then denied again by Ranson late on, before Charlie Seaman’s shot was deflected over for a corner as Billericay dug in to defend their point.
The game’s final act saw a Fleet corner cleared only as far as Kwesi Appiah, but his goalbound strike was blocked by George Wind before Town cleared to earn a valuable point on the road.
Danny Scopes’ side continue their impressive unbeaten run and remain in the play-off places, and are next in action when Horsham visit Pulse Stadium New Lodge on Saturday.

Billericay Town: Ranson; Wind, Scott, Lomas, Porter; Clark, Watts; Long (Ferdinand 63), Ruff (Tripp 69), Benton; Merrifield (Mauge 78)
Subs not used: Brown, Martin Sorondo, Appiah, Parsons
Referee: Jack Bloxham
Attendance: 1,029 (122 away)

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Billericay Town 4 Slough Town 1
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Billericay Town 4 (Benton 12, Watts 20, Thomas OG 26, Merrifield 49) – Slough Town 1 (Spencer 54)
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Stefan Sheriden Photofold Camera Club
Jon Benton produced another superb individual performance as Billericay Town cruised past basement side Slough Town at Pulse Stadium New Lodge.
The Blues had the game’s first chance on six minutes when Ryan Scott glanced a header wide from Benton’s cross.
Town broke the deadlock on 12 minutes when Benton latched onto Charlie Ruff’s pinpoint through ball before beating Killian Barrett.
The lead was doubled eight minutes later when Callum Watts’ initial shot was saved by Barrett, but the midfielder managed to find a gap between the defender and goalkeeper to score at the second attempt.
Benton was then heavily involved again as Billericay made it three, with his low cross being turned into his own net by the unfortunate Terell Thomas.
Slough struggled to cause the hosts any problems but did have a handball appeal waved away when the ball struck Watts following a corner.
Billericay had a big chance to make it four on 31 minutes when Elliot Long was denied by a last-ditch challenge from Joseph Morrison, before Benton’s follow-up effort was saved by Barrett.
The visitors finished the half on top, with Dennon Lewis having a shot held by Khari Ranson before firing wide of the post in first-half stoppage time, though Billericay’s commanding lead remained intact at the break.
The Blues immediately set about extending their advantage in the second half, with Ruff trying his luck with a spectacular volley, only for Barrett to keep him out.
The fourth goal arrived four minutes after the break when Ruff’s free-kick was nodded down by Louis Lomas, allowing Frankie Merrifield to turn home from close range.
Slough got one back on 54 minutes when a well-worked move down the right flank ended with Shay Spencer picking out the far corner.
The visitors saw more of the ball in the second half, with a deflected shot from substitute Jaiden Drakes-Thomas going past the upright 20 minutes from time.
Benton then came close to adding to his tally in quick succession, first seeing a shot pushed over by Barrett before striking the post after a brilliant individual run.
The Blues had the final chance of the afternoon when Sebastian Ferdinand’s curling effort sailed just over the bar, but the result had long since been settled as Billericay picked up another three points.
Town remain unbeaten at home in the league and make the trip to league leaders Ebbsfleet United on Tuesday night.

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Truro City 0 Billericay Town 0
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Truro City 0 – Billericay Town 0
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Jon Bird
Danny Scopes’ Billericay Town side produced a heroic defensive performance to earn a point on a wet and windy night in Cornwall against Truro City.
The home side immediately set about putting Billericay under pressure, and Luke Jephcott was brilliantly denied by Khari Ranson after Christian Oxlade-Chamberlain’s long throw caused havoc in the box.
Billericay ventured forward for the first time on nine minutes and saw a looping header from Elliot Long drop wide of the post.
Truro continued to have most of the play in the first half, with Jephcott again combining with Oxlade-Chamberlain, but the latter saw his header go just over the bar.
Town found chances hard to come by in the opening 45 minutes but put together their best move of the game on 36 minutes, though Callum Watts couldn’t keep his shot down from the edge of the box.
The Tinners dominated the final minutes of the half, and Ranson was called into action to claim multiple crosses and deal with Tyler Harvey’s header a minute before the break, ensuring it stayed level.
The second half started in dire conditions, with torrential rain and strong winds, though the hosts played on despite the weather and saw Jephcott fire just over the bar from 18 yards.
Billericay remained a danger on the break and saw a rare flurry into the box end with Jon Benton’s shot sailing over the top of Aidan Stone’s bar.
Truro’s best chance came on 65 minutes when Harvey’s header released Harvey Greenslade, but he dragged his shot wide with only Ranson to beat.
Taylor Clark then fired over at the other end as the game became stretched heading into the final 20 minutes.
City put Billericay under immense pressure in the closing stages with countless long throws from Oxlade-Chamberlain and set pieces, but Ranson and the Town back four stood up to the task well and denied any clear-cut chances.
The only chance the hosts mustered from this pressure came on 89 minutes, though Harvey’s header was straight into the hands of Ranson.
Billericay then had two chances of their own to snatch all three points in stoppage time, first when Jamie Mauge broke away only to be denied by a brilliant challenge from Jephcott.
And from the final corner in the game’s dying seconds, Paul Appiah’s goalbound shot was somehow cleared off the line by Jephcott before the referee’s whistle brought an end to an attritional contest.
The Blues move to ten league games unbeaten following the draw in Cornwall and welcome basement side Slough Town to Essex on Saturday afternoon.
Truro City: Stone; Oxlade-Chamberlain, Harrison, Law; Tweedy, W. Dean, Jephcott, Riley-Lowe; T. Dean, Harvey, Greenslade (Dennis 69)
Subs not used: Lavercombe, Donnellan, Colwell, Kinsey
Billericay Town: Ranson; Wind, Scott, Lomas, Porter; Tripp (Martin Sorondo 68), Clark; Long, Watts (Ferdinand 75), Benton (Mauge 86); Merrifield (Appiah 90+2)
Subs not used: Brown, Parsons
Referee: Jonathan Bolland
Attendance: 1,462

https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.title: Billericay Town 3 Waltham Abbey 1
https://www.billericaytownfc.co.uk/feed/.text:
Billericay Town 3 (Mauge 22, Benton 84, 86 pen) – Waltham Abbey 1 (Cawley 42)
Match report by Ben Mapp
Match photos by Stephen Mold of Photofold Camera Club
Jon Benton’s second brace of the week helped Billericay Town overcome a resolute Waltham Abbey side and progress to the last 64 of the FA Trophy at Pulse Stadium New Lodge.
The Step 4 visitors started the brighter and saw a shot from top scorer Prince William Domafriyie well saved by Khari Ranson in the Town goal.
Billericay’s first chance of the afternoon came on 11 minutes when Benton’s shot was deflected wide off an Abbey defender.
The away side thought they had taken the lead ten minutes later when an inswinging corner was fumbled by Ranson and dropped into the net, though referee Tommy Flemming ruled the goal out for a foul.
The Blues took the lead a minute later when Benton burst down the flank and crossed for Ipswich loanee Jamie Mauge to tap home his first Billericay goal.
Town looked for an immediate second and saw Benton weave into the box before firing just wide of the upright.
The Abbotts responded and twice forced Ranson into action with efforts from distance, the second coming from Maxwell Appauh, with the Billericay keeper pushing his shot wide.
From the resulting corner, Abbey levelled. Although the initial delivery was dealt with, Steve Cawley was on hand to turn home from close range after the ball was recycled into the area.
Billericay had a golden chance to regain the lead on 45 minutes when Mauge’s header was somehow saved by Hafed Al Droubi, before the visiting keeper then denied Elliot Long’s follow-up to ensure it was level at the interval.
The second half was delayed due to a medical incident in the crowd, with the half-time break lasting nearly 45 minutes before the sides took part in a short warm-up and the action resumed.
Town dominated possession early in the half and thought they should have had a penalty when Ryan Scott’s header struck an arm, though the officials were unmoved despite loud Billericay appeals.
The Blues continued to press for a second, seeing a shot from Benton saved by Al Droubi and Charlie Ruff’s dipping volley fall the wrong side of the post.
Waltham Abbey struggled to create chances in the second half, though they did fashion an opening that saw Appauh blaze over from inside the box on 70 minutes, before Aiden Read headed over the bar eight minutes later.
Billericay went ahead six minutes from time when some neat footwork from Benton saw him create space in the box before wrong-footing Al Droubi and finding the bottom corner.
Two minutes later, he had his second and his side’s third when Ruff was felled in the box, allowing Benton to step up and convert from 12 yards to ensure Billericay’s progression into Round Three.
Town are now unbeaten in eight games in all competitions and make the long trip to Truro City on Tuesday evening.
Billericay Town: Ranson; Wind, Scott, Parsons (Lomas 58), Porter; Martin Sorondo (Tripp 62), Watts; Long (Ferdinand 72), Ruff, Benton; Mauge (Merrifield 72)
Subs not used: Appiah
Waltham Abbey: Al Droubi; Robbins, Knight, Read, Taylor; Barker (Williams 81), Pedro; William Domafriyie (Stevenson 71), Blower (Velasco 46), Appauh (Rookard 87); Cawley
Subs not used: Galliford
Referee: Tommy Flemming
Attendance: 849.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Game Preview: Essex Rebels Movember Doubleheader | 28 November
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
This Saturday marks another Super League Basketball and British Championship Basketball doubleheader which is in partnership with Movemeber UK.
Essex Rebels Women vs B.Braun Sheffield Hatters | 4pm Tip-off
The Essex Rebels Women are back at the Essex Sport Arena this Saturday after 3 weeks which included a 2-week FIBA International Break.
Freeman’s last game saw an important 88-80 win to Nottingham Wildcats. This sits the Rebels 7 th in the league and will be looking for a crucial 2 points in hopes to move up the table.
However, this will not be an easy task for the Rebels as they face the successful Sheffield Hatters who currently sit four places above them in 3 rd .
Vanessa Ellis’ side enjoyed a quadruple winning season last year, winning the Super League and earning herself Coach of the Year.
Working to defend their title, Sheffield have currently registered 5 out of 7 wins this season hitting a lull at the start of the season hitting back-to-back losses against Manchester and Oaklands. But they are currently on a 4-game winning streak, most recently beating Leicester Riders 93-82 just last weekend.
Player to Watch: Nina Krisper
Nina Krisper is one to keep an eye on for the visitors this weekend. The Australian forward is in her third consecutive season for the Hatters, playing a pivotal role in the team’s championship run last season.  Krisper has continued her incredible form this season, currently she has registered an average of 18.3 points, 7.9 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game, ranking first in her team for both points and rebounds and in the top four for assists. Marking Krisper defensively will be key to ensure a Rebels’ success.
Essex Rebels Men vs London Cavaliers | 6:30pm Tip-off
Following the women’s game, British Championship Basketball will resume at the Essex Sport Arena as the Rebels host London Cavaliers.
The Rebels are entering the game off the back of two consecutive wins against Nottingham Hoods and Milton Keynes Breakers.  Perkins’ side walked away with a 98-92 win against the Breakers, with Aliou Cisse playing an essential role in the Rebels’ victory.
Cisse earned himself British Championship Player of the Week after an incredible performance of 32 points, 7 rebounds and 3 blocks. Alongside Cisse, dynamic duo Tre Baumgardner and Kyron Martin also enjoyed a successful game against the Breakers, between them registering 39 points and 22 assists. The attacking trio will look to continue this form and extend their winning streak this weekend.
The Rebels visited London for the reverse fixture just a month ago. The Rebels fell short on the road by 104-82 and will be looking to settle the score on Saturday.
The Cavaliers will not make it an easy game as they will be fighting to get back on track as they come into this weekend off the back off an 85-61 defeat to Birmingham Rockets.
Player to Watch: Juan Manning
A player to watch for the Cavaliers is combo guard Juan Manning.  Manning will look to bring his impressive scoring ability to the Arena this weekend after already registering 21.4 points, 4.6 assists and 0.9 blocks per game this season.
Manning ranks first in his team for all three aspects making him an all-round performer that the Rebels will need to watch to be in with a chance of seeking revenge of the Cavaliers.
Tickets are still available, so be sure not to miss out on this incredible afternoon of live basketball action all in the name of Movember.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Men Claim First Victory Under Joshua Perkins in Thrilling Comeback Win
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Rebels Men secure their first win under recently appointed head coach, Joshua Perkins in a dramatic contest that went down to the wire.
Having played Nottingham just a month earlier and fallen to a narrow 79-77 defeat, the Rebels were determined to avenge the defeat and claim the important two points.
It was the Rebels who got off the mark first courtesy of a lay-up from Tyresse Hudson. Hudson’s early basket set the tone for a strong first quarter with the Rebels enjoying a good run of team play seeing contributions across the board from Ethan Conway, Tre Baumgardner and Michael Amako. Despite the visitors following the Rebels closely throughout the quarter due to a great performance from Cameron Kahn, it was the Rebels who took the lead after the opening 10 minutes holding a scoreline of 24-19.
The second quarter began in much of the same fashion. Tre Baumgardner continued his formidable form this season as he added 5 points in the opening 30 second extending the Rebels’ lead by 10.
However, around the mid-point of the quarter momentum began to swing in Nottingham’s favour. Tactical substitutions from the Hoods proved effective seeing Christian Moore and Camden Polak make an impact on the game closing the deficit and levelling the scores at 37-37.
After evening the scoreline, the Hoods continued to thrive heading into halftime, narrowly taking a 49-45 lead at the half-way point.
The third quarter continued to work in Nottingham’s favour producing their strongest spell of the game. Polak continued to dictate proceedings whilst Elliot Bailey came into the game contributing seven valuable points.
The Hoods led 80-68 heading into the final quarter but with Tre Baumgardner continuing his outstanding run this game, it was not an impossible task for the Rebels in the final quarter.
The final quarter brought the drama as momentum continued to swing back and forth. Free throws and a lay-up from Harry Gent allowed the Rebels to creep up on their visitors reducing the deficit to just 7 with four minutes left on the clock.
As the clock continued to run down, Baumgardner hit the hoops to level the score to 96-96. With just 38 seconds left overtime looked on the horizon, but Baumgarner was fouled and two free throws were awarded.
After rolling round the rim of the basket, the first free throw was missed. With everything riding on this throw, pressure was rising. Making the buzzer-beating shot Baumgardner became the hero as he secured the Rebels’ their two points and their first win since the beginning of the October.
As well as securing the win, Tre Baumgardner’s performance earned himself Player of the Match with 38 points, 4 rebounds and 8 assists.
The Rebels will hope to continue this form next weekend as they travel to Milton Keynes before returning to the Essex Sport Arena on the 28 November to face London Cavaliers.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Seek Revenge Against Nottingham Hoods
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels return to the Essex Sport Arena on Saturday 14 November with one thing on their minds: revenge.
Just a month ago, the Rebels suffered a narrow 79-77 defeat on the road against the Nottingham Hoods in a game that could have gone either way. Despite a spirited performance from Essex led by Aliou Cisse who finished with 29 points, the Hoods edged the contest late on, leaving the Rebels eager to even the score on home court this weekend.

The Rebels will need to tighten up defensively and limit Nottingham’s scoring options if they are to come away with the win.
Essex enters the contest looking to snap a difficult run of late, having lost five consecutive games. However, with home support behind them and plenty of motivation following last month’s heartbreak, the Rebels will be determined to return to winning ways.
Led by the dynamic duo of Tre Baumgardner and Aliou Cisse, the Rebels will be hoping to deliver a strong response and secure a statement victory as they continue their push up the standings.
With the memory of the two-point defeat still fresh, all the ingredients are in place for an exciting contest between two sides with plenty to prove.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Men Fall on the Road to Worthing
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels fell 109-96 to Worthing Thunder despite an encouraging opening half that saw the visitors establish an early advantage and remain in contention through the opening twenty minutes.
The Rebels started brightly through Tre Baumgardner III who led the early scoring charge, knocking down back-to-back three-pointers in a 30 second period. Melchi Egbeyemi and Kyron Martin also enjoyed a successful spell which helped the Rebels build a narrow 30-26 lead at the end of the first quarter.
Essex continued to build momentum early in the second period, extending to an 8-point lead in the first two minutes. However, the momentum shifted dramatically later in the quarter when Worthing began to find their rhythm through Justin Hopkins and Manuel Hernandez, who combined to spark a strong run.
Hernandez repeatedly attacked the basket while Hopkins provided scoring both inside and outside the Arc. The hosts finished the half strongly to overturn the deficit and take a 59-49 lead into the break.
The decisive stretch arrived in the third quarter. Worthing’s offence exploded, with Hernandez, Craig and Ostrowsky all making major contributions. Punishing the Rebels defence, Worthing headed into the final quarter leading by 20 at 89-69.
Determined to make a comeback, the Rebels started the fourth quarter with a renewed energy, reducing the deficit to just 13 in the first two minutes. Baumgardner, Conway and Martin all connected to make crucial baskets to help reduce the deficit.
Despite the Rebels determination, Worthing continued to capitalise on the counter to ensure they kept their lead. A driving lay-up from Hernadez with 20 seconds on the clock, capped off a strong performance from the hosts who secured a 109-96 victory.
Perkins’ side will look to comeback from this defeat as they return home to the Essex Sport Arena next weekend as they host Nottingham Hoods on Saturday 14 November with a 6:30 Tip-off.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Rebels Women Secure Away Win Against Nottingham
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
The Essex Rebels take two points on the road as they secure an 88-80 win against the Nottingham Wildcats.
Tor Freeman’s side got back on track as they walked away with their second win of the Super League Basketball season this weekend.
After facing back-to-back losses to Manchester and Newcastle at home, the Rebels travelled to Nottingham to face the Wildcats, determined to turn their season around.
The hosts made a bright start immediately establishing control as they took a 12-5 advantage in the opening three minutes. However, at the midway point of the opening quarter the Rebels began to close the deficit with Olivia Forster acting as a catalyst. Forster’s 3-point jump shot came with 4 minutes on the clock and sparked successful spells from JaMya Robinson and Alexa Mikeska whose lay-ups gave the Rebels their first lead of the game.
This spur of momentum handed the Rebels a 26-22 advantage at the end of the first quarter.  The Rebels continued to stretch their advantage throughout the second quarter. Forster and Robinson continued their impressive form ensuring Rebels capitalised on the Wildcats’ mistake. Contributions also came from Lara Rohkohl and Alexa Mikeska who continued to work hard offensively and defensively.  The Rebels walked into half time ahead, extending their lead to 55-44.
The Rebels were determined to maintain their lead after half time. Whilst Rohkohl enjoyed an influential spell, the visitors endured their quietest offensive period of the game, working hard on the defence to ensure Nottingham were kept at bay.
Nottingham attempted to mount a comeback in the final quarter, Davids-Oboh and Basham helped the hosts reduce the deficit to single digits for the first time since the first quarter. Despite the Wildcats enjoying their strongest spell, consecutive 3-pointers from Rebels captain Claire Paxton halted Nottingham’s momentum.
As the clock wound down, the Rebels continued to apply the pressure. Alexa Mikeska stood out as she dominated defensively with key rebounds and steals which helped the Rebels maintain control in the closing stages.
Mikeska influence not only ensured the Rebels walked away with an 88-80 win, she also earned herself Player of the Match after registering a double-double in assists and 2 rebounds off a triple-double after adding a tally of 14 points, 8 rebounds 12 assists and 5 steals.
The Rebels will look to continue this form after the international break. Freeman’s Rebels will return to the Essex Sport Arena on 28 November where they will host the Braun Sheffield Hatters.

https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.title: Essex Rebels Fall Short to the Eagles by a Single Point.
https://www.essexrebels.co.uk/feed/.text:
Essex Rebels Women endured a narrow 83-82 loss against Newcastle Eagles at the Essex Sport Arena.
The final scoreline reflected a tightly contested game, with momentum swinging between both sides from start to finish.
The opening quarter quickly set the tone for what proved to be a closely fought battle. Despite the Eagles getting off to the perfect start through summer signing Raven Thompson, who opened the scoring with a three-point jump shot, consecutive lay-ups from Rebels star Lara Rohkohl immediately levelled the scores.
With two minutes left on the clock, Claire Paxton fired the Rebels two points ahead, handing the hosts their first lead of the contest. The visitors, however, responded with a three-pointer of their own and carried that advantage into the closing stages of the quarter, leading 23-20 after the opening ten minutes.
The second quarter unfolded in much of the same fashion, with the lead changing hands repeatedly. Rohkohl remained influential throughout, scoring 10 points in the period. But the Eagles consistently found answers through Nala Williams and Alex Campbell whose efforts helped Newcastle edge into a narrow 40-39 lead at the half-time break.
The visitors produced their strongest spell of the game during the third quarter, opening their largest advantage of the evening as they built a seven-point lead.
However, the Rebels responded emphatically in the closing stages, with three consecutive three-pointers, two from Olivia Partridge and one from Cameron Taylor-Willis, halting the Eagles’ momentum and cutting the deficit to just two points heading into the final quarter at 64-62.
With the game finely poised, the Rebels seized control early in the fourth. Paxton caught fire from beyond the arc while Rohkohl continued to dominate at both ends of the floor, helping Essex establish a five-point advantage midway through the period.
Newcastle, however, produced a late surge, capitalising on second-chance opportunities and key defensive plays to claw their way back in front.
Despite Paxton drilling a buzzer-beating three-pointer to leave the Rebels just one point behind, the Eagles held on to secure a dramatic 83-82 victory.
The Rebels will travel to Nottingham next weekend to face Nottingham Wildcats.

https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.text:
Great Dunmow Town Council Completes Transfer of Brick Kiln Farm Open Space
Great Dunmow Town Council is pleased to announce that the transfer of the public open space at Brick Kiln Farm has now been completed and ownership of the land has passed to the Town Council. The transfer has been completed by the parties and submitted to HM Land Registry for formal registration.
The acquisition forms part of the long-standing planning obligations associated with the Brick Kiln Farm development and secures the open space as a community asset for the benefit of residents of Great Dunmow.
The transfer brings to completion a process that began with the submission of planning application UTT/13/0847/OP in July 2013. The application proposed the demolition of three dwellings, associated outbuildings and derelict farm buildings, and the construction of up to 68 dwellings together with associated infrastructure and approximately 9.4 hectares of public open space. The accompanying Section 106 Agreement required the developer to offer the public open space to Great Dunmow Town Council for transfer, with the land to be retained and managed for the recreational use and enjoyment of the general public.
In addition to the transfer of the land, a commuted maintenance sum has been received to support the future upkeep and management of the site.
The Council would like to thank all those involved in bringing the transfer to completion and looks forward to managing and enhancing the open space for the enjoyment of current and future generations.
Amanda Alexander, the Town Clerk, said:
“We are delighted that this important transfer has now been completed. The open space is a valuable community asset, and the Council is committed to ensuring it is maintained and managed for the benefit of residents both now and in the future.”
Further information regarding the future management of the site will be provided as plans are developed.
Amanda Alexander
Town Clerk
Great Dunmow Town Council

https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.title: PLANNING DEADLINE CLARIFICATION
https://greatdunmow-tc.gov.uk/feed/.text:
Broadway Planning Response Deadline Clarification
UDC’s Website
Uttlesford District Council`s website states:
Neighbour consultation expiry date is Monday 24th August
Latest consultation expiry date is Wednesday 12th August
Town Council response
For a town council, the statutory deadline is the earliest of the published consultation dates, the “latest consultation expiry date” (12/08/26) not the neighbour consultation date of 24/08/26.
Latest consultation expiry date 12/08/26
This is the formal public consultation period under the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) Order.
It is the date used for statutory consultees, including town and parish councils.
Latest neighbour consultation date 24/08/26
This is the deadline for neighbours who received letters. Councils are not treated as neighbours: they are statutory consultees.
Town and Parish Councils must work to the formal consultation expiry date unless the Local Planning Authority explicitly extends the consultee period in writing.
Comments can still be submitted after the official deadline, LPAs often accept late representations, but they are not guaranteed to be taken into account.
Residents who are not neighbours, but wish to respond to the application
Residents who are not neighbours and did not receive letters from Uttlesford District Council should use the formal consultation expiry date (12/08/26) as their deadline.
Comments submitted on or before 12/08/26 are guaranteed to be treated as valid.
Comments submitted after this date are usually still accepted, but the case officer is not obliged to consider them.
If a resident wants to be absolutely safe, they should treat 12/08/26 as the deadline.
